posts.title: It's Official
posts.content:
It's been five months since we met and almost two months since I became your suitor. And with that small span of time—from days to weeks, until it eventually turned into months—it's still such a short amount of time, but somehow, it feels like we've been together for years. It's fascinating how someone can become such a familiar part of your life in such a little time, how conversations slowly turn into routines, how the smallest updates become something you look forward to every day, and how an ordinary moment can suddenly feel so much more meaningful simply because you get to share it with that one person. I never really understood how people could feel so comfortable with someone in such a short amount of time, but then you came along, and I found myself experiencing exactly that. It's as if we've known each other long before our paths crossed, as if there's a certain familiarity between us that makes everything feel so natural, and as if loving you has become one of the easiest things my heart has ever learned to do.

I guess that's what happens when you find someone who feels like home, someone whose presence you eventually become accustomed to, not because you get tired of having them around, but because having them in your everyday life becomes something you genuinely cherish. You don't really count the days anymore; instead, you find yourself looking forward to all the little things that come with having them around, whether it's hearing about how their day went, listening to their random stories, sharing the most insignificant details, or simply knowing that somewhere in the middle of everything happening in your separate lives, you still have each other to come home to. And somewhere along the way, without either of us noticing just how much things were changing, we started building something that neither of us wanted to let go of.

And yes—you said yes to me. Exactly at 12:18 AM on November 3, you said, "We're official."

I didn't get you at first, but then you explained and explained until I slowly understood what you were trying to tell me, and it's been an hour since it finally sank in on me. I was genuinely flabbergasted because, what do you mean we were just crying before you said yes to me? What do you mean I had been feeling so much pressure just a while ago, opening up to you and telling you everything that had been weighing on my mind? What do you mean we were both feeling so down, trying to figure things out and comfort one another, and then, in just a snap, we suddenly turned into this lively, lovey-dovey couple who couldn't stop expressing how happy we were? I swear, if someone had told me that this was how our night would end, I probably would've laughed because I couldn't have imagined that a night that started with so many emotions would eventually become one of the nights I'd want to remember for the rest of my life.

How does a night go from holding back tears to holding onto something we've both been waiting for? How can two people who were just trying to make sense of their feelings suddenly find themselves celebrating a new chapter of their relationship? It's almost amusing when I think about it, but at the same time, there's something so beautiful about how everything unfolded. We didn't have to plan for the perfect moment, prepare ourselves for some grand confession, or wait until everything around us was completely settled before we could finally have this conversation. It just happened, in the middle of an ordinary night, after an honest conversation, through all the explanations, reassurances, and emotions that came with it. And perhaps that's what makes it even more special to me, because it wasn't some perfectly orchestrated moment; it was simply us, being ourselves, figuring things out together, and somehow finding our way into something we've both been looking forward to.

But perhaps that's one of the things I love most about us: we don't always have to be at our happiest to find something beautiful in each other, and we don't have to pretend that everything is okay just to keep things light between us. We can have difficult conversations, cry when things become overwhelming, admit when we're scared or uncertain, and still find comfort in knowing that neither of us has to face those feelings alone. I want you to know that you don't have to be the happiest version of yourself whenever you're with me, because I want to be there for the days when you're feeling a little less like yourself, too. I want to understand the things you sometimes struggle to explain, listen to the stories you keep repeating, reassure you when your thoughts become too loud, and remind you that you are loved even on the days when you find it difficult to feel that way. I don't want our relationship to become a place where we only celebrate the good things; I want it to be a place where we can also be honest about the difficult ones.

I know that becoming official doesn't automatically mean that everything will suddenly be perfect, that we'll never misunderstand each other, or that we'll always know exactly what to say whenever one of us is having a difficult time. There will still be days when we're tired, days when our schedules don't align, days when we have different perspectives, and days when life becomes a little too overwhelming for either of us, but I hope that through all of those things, we never lose the willingness to understand one another, communicate even when it's uncomfortable, apologize when we've made mistakes, and choose to be gentle with each other even when things aren't as easy as we'd like them to be. I don't expect us to have everything figured out right away, and I don't expect either of us to be perfect partners, because we're both still learning, growing, and discovering what it means to love someone in ways that make them feel understood and appreciated.

I don't want us to rush through this just because we finally have a label to call what we've been building for the past few months, because I still want to experience everything with you at our own pace, without feeling like we have to accomplish every little milestone immediately just because we're finally here. I want the ordinary days, the random conversations that somehow last for hours, the little dates that we'll probably talk about even after they happen, the laughter over things that nobody else would understand, the quiet moments when we don't necessarily have to say anything, and even the difficult conversations that teach us how to love each other better. I want to keep learning about you, discovering the little things you haven't told me yet, understanding the different sides of you that I haven't had the chance to meet, and falling in love with every version of you that I get to encounter as we grow older and experience more of life together. I want to be someone you can celebrate your achievements with, someone you can lean on when things become difficult, and someone who will always remind you that you don't have to figure everything out on your own.

And now, I get to call you my girlfriend. My love, my favorite person, my someone. I get to introduce you as the woman I love, and I get to look forward to all the little things that come with being able to call this relationship ours. God, it still feels so unreal typing those words, especially when I think about how everything started, how we went from getting to know each other to becoming each other's constant, and how the person I once hoped would say yes to me is now someone I can proudly call my girlfriend. If only I could go back to the beginning and tell the version of myself who was still gathering the courage to pursue you that one day, after all the conversations, the uncertainties, the reassurances, and the little moments we would eventually collect, I would get to call you mine, I think that version of me would have the biggest smile on their face.

Five months ago, we were just two people who happened to cross paths, almost two months ago, I gathered the courage to pursue you and show you how much I wanted to get to know you beyond what we already shared, and today, November 3, we get to look back at all those little moments and realize that they somehow led us here. It's funny how time works, because although it hasn't been that long since we first met, I already have so many memories with you that I want to keep close to my heart, and now that we're officially together, I can't help but feel excited about all the memories we haven't made yet, all the places we haven't visited, all the conversations we haven't had, and all the little milestones that are still waiting for us somewhere in the future.

I hope you know how happy I am that it's you and how grateful I am that, out of all the possibilities life could have given us, somehow, we found each other at the right time and decided to give this a chance. I know there are still so many things ahead of us, and I know we'll encounter moments that will challenge our patience, understanding, and commitment, but I hope we continue to find reasons to stay, reasons to communicate, and reasons to fall in love with each other all over again. I hope that years from now, when we look back at November 3, we'll remember how an ordinary night, filled with tears and conversations, unexpectedly became the night we officially started calling each other girlfriends, and we'll laugh about how I couldn't even understand what was happening at first because I was too overwhelmed to process that you had finally said yes.

So, here's to us, my love. Here's to the beginning of something we've already been taking care of for months, to the little things that brought us closer, to the love that continues to grow between us, and to all the versions of ourselves we'll get to meet as we navigate this relationship together. Here's to more firsts, more memories, more dates, more late-night conversations, more laughter, more reassurance, and more ordinary days that will eventually become some of our most treasured memories. I may not know exactly what the future has prepared for us, but I know that I want to keep experiencing it with you, one day at a time, without rushing through the beautiful things we're still about to discover.

It's official. You're my girlfriend, and I'm yours. And if there's one thing I want you to remember from all of this, it's that I didn't just want to become your girlfriend; I wanted to become someone you could continue choosing, trusting, growing with, and loving through every season of life. Thank you for saying yes to me, for allowing me to love you in this way, and for giving us the chance to turn everything we've been building into something we can finally call ours.

I love you so much, Asaiah Ysabel. Here's to us, and hopefully, to a lifetime of being each other's favorite person.

posts.title: Happy Birthday, My Love!!
posts.content:
Happy birthday to the plot twist that i never expected—to the woman i love.

If someone told me before that one day, someone would come into my life so unexpectedly and somehow become one of the most important parts of it, I probably wouldn't have believed them. I never planned for you, never knew I was looking for someone like you, and yet somehow, life brought you to me at the most unexpected time.

And now, here we are.

Another year of your life, and i feel incredibly lucky that i get to witness it. I get to know the little things about you, listen to your stories, hear your voice, see your smile, and be there through the good days and the days when everything feels a little heavier. I get to love you not just on the days when you're at your happiest but also on the days when you need someone to remind you that you don't have to carry everything alone.

I hope this birthday reminds you of how deeply loved you are—not only by me, but by the people whose lives you've touched just by being yourself. I hope you know how much warmth you bring into the lives around you, even when you don't realize you're doing it.

And selfishly, I hope you know how much you mean to me.

You have become my comfort, my favorite person to talk to, my little piece of peace in the middle of everything. somewhere along the way, the person I never expected became the person I find myself wanting to choose, again and again.

So on your birthday, I don't just wish you happiness. I wish you a life that feels gentle. I wish for you dreams that come true, days that don't feel too heavy, and people who will always make you feel safe, seen, and loved. I hope this new chapter gives you more reasons to smile, more moments worth remembering, and more opportunities to become the woman you've always wanted to be.

And if you'll let me, I want to be there for as much of it as you’ll have me.

Happy birthday, my love. Thank you for being the most unexpected plot twist in my life—and somehow, the one I never want to write out of the story.

posts.title: The Days I Started Counting
posts.subtitle: On meeting you, choosing you, and never wanting to stop knowing you.
posts.content:
Does counting days or months matter?

I'm not really sure if it does. I used to think time was just time—something that passes whether we pay attention to it or not. But then I caught myself counting.

I started counting from the day I asked if I could court you. Two months since that question left my mouth. Three months since the night we first met. Three months since you were still a stranger whose name I didn't know would eventually become something I would look for in the middle of my day.

It's strange how quickly those numbers arrived.

Two months.

Three months.

They sound small when I say them out loud. Almost insignificant compared to how long people usually take to know someone. But when I think about everything that has happened within those months, I don't think of them as small anymore.

I think of all the ordinary days that somehow became worth remembering.

The conversations that stretched longer than they were supposed to. The moments when I learned something new about you without even realizing I was keeping it somewhere in my mind. The things you've said in passing that stayed with me long after the conversation ended. The parts of your personality that slowly became familiar—not because I tried to study you, but because paying attention to you started feeling natural.

Maybe that's why I started counting.

Not because I need a number to prove how long I've loved you.

Not because two months or three months suddenly makes what I feel more valid.

I think I count because sometimes I can't believe how much can happen between one date and another.

Three months ago, I didn't know you.

Two months ago, I asked if you would let me try to know you in a different way.

And now, here I am, somehow remembering things about you that I never thought I would care enough to remember.

I remember the way you phrase certain things. The little habits you've mentioned. The preferences you've casually revealed. The things you get excited about. The things that make you tired. The moments when you become quieter. The moments when your personality fills the entire conversation.

I don't think I intentionally memorized any of it.

It just stayed.

That's the strange thing about getting attached to someone. You don't always notice when the details start becoming familiar. There isn't a specific moment when you realize, Oh, I know this about her now.

One day, you simply know.

You know what kind of answer she might give. You recognize the little changes in the way she talks. You remember something she mentioned weeks ago without having to make an effort. You notice when something sounds different from usual.

And suddenly, you realize you've been paying attention all along.

I didn't just memorize you.

I memorized the person you are.

And maybe that's different.

Because people change. The version of you I met three months ago isn't going to be exactly the same person I know months from now. There will be things about you that shift with time, things you'll outgrow, things you'll discover about yourself, things you might eventually see differently.

And I don't want to hold you to the version I first met.

I want to have the privilege of seeing what comes after her.

Who you'll become when your life changes. What you'll believe in years from now. What you'll eventually want for yourself. Which dreams will stay and which ones you'll replace with something you never expected to want.

Maybe that's why the idea of knowing you feels so much more exciting to me than the idea of having you completely figured out.

Because I don't think I ever want to reach a point where I can say, I already know everything about you.

That sounds less like love to me and more like the end of curiosity.

And I don't want my curiosity about you to end.

I don't want to know you completely. I want to know you continuously—to keep meeting the versions of you that time brings, and to never run out of reasons to be curious about the person you're becoming.

I won't lie and say that memorizing someone is easy. Sometimes I probably get things wrong. Sometimes I misunderstand. Sometimes I think I know what you're thinking and realize I was completely wrong.

But even that doesn't make me want to stop.

If anything, it reminds me that you're a person, not a puzzle I'm supposed to solve.

You're allowed to surprise me.

You're allowed to change your mind.

You're allowed to become someone I didn't predict.

You're allowed to have parts of yourself that I haven't reached yet.

And maybe I'll always be a little curious about those parts.

I think I'm more in love with the possibility of knowing you than with the comfort of thinking I already do.

Because knowing you isn't supposed to have an ending.

There will always be another conversation, another season, another version of you I haven't encountered yet. There will be days when I'll understand you immediately and days when I won't. There will be things you'll tell me years from now that I couldn't possibly know today.

And somehow, I like that.

I like that there is still so much life ahead of us that neither of us can predict.

So yes, maybe counting does matter to me after all.

Not because I'm keeping score.

Not because I'm waiting for a certain number of months to make what we have feel more important.

I count because each number reminds me that time is actually moving.

Three months since we met.

Two months since I asked you.

And however many days have passed since then, I know I've spent them becoming more certain that knowing you is something I never want to take for granted.

Maybe someday, I'll stop counting.

Maybe the months will blur together, and I'll forget the exact number of days between one milestone and another.

But I hope I'll never forget what those numbers meant when they were still new.

Three months was when I realized a stranger could become someone familiar.

Two months was when I chose to take a chance on whatever this could become.

And today is another day I get to know you a little more than I did yesterday.

Maybe that's enough.

Maybe I don't need to know how many days it will take.

I just know that, for as long as I'm given the chance, I want to keep meeting every version of you that time introduces me to.

Written in the quiet hours, mostly for me—and now, for you too.
Cathlynn.

posts.title: A Diary for Two
posts.subtitle: The pages I never knew would belong to us.
posts.content:
I didn't know that my website, If No One Reads This, would eventually be filled with letters for you.

It was originally a space entirely for me—my thoughts I couldn't say out loud, feelings and emotions I didn't know what to do with, and a little corner of the internet where I could write simply because I needed to write. It was never meant to be about anyone else. I wasn't thinking about who would read it, who would understand it, or whether anyone would ever find meaning in the words I left there.

Little did I know that you would slowly find your way into those pages.

What started as a website for myself somehow became part of you, too. It became a diary for two, even though I never planned for it to be one. There are letters about how we met, about the night our conversations began, about asking you if you'd let me court you and see where this could go. There are pieces about the person you are becoming, the future version of you I'm curious to meet, and even the little girl you once were—the one I never had the chance to know but somehow still want to understand through the woman you've become.

And somewhere along the way, I realized something about what this website had become:

Maybe I started writing because I needed somewhere to put my thoughts, but somewhere between one page and another, you became part of the reason I kept writing. What was once a place where I only left pieces of myself slowly became a place where I could leave pieces of us, too.

That's the irony of its name, If No One Reads This.

At first, I genuinely didn't care if anyone ever saw these words. I wrote because writing was enough. I didn't need an audience. I didn't need anyone to understand. But then I met someone who made me want these words to reach her.

You.

The website became a timeline of us without me ever meaning for it to. Each new piece became a small marker of where we were, who we were, and what I was feeling at that particular moment. Some entries came from conversations we had. Some came from things you said without realizing how deeply they stayed with me. Some came from moments I wanted to remember because I knew they would eventually become memories.

It's still my website. These are still my thoughts, my words, my little corner of the internet.

But the story behind so many of them belongs to both of us.

And it isn't just the website that somehow became a diary for two. My other accounts did, too.

I never intentionally decided that I wanted my accounts to be filled with you. I didn't sit down one day and think, I'm going to make this account about her. It just happened. A picture here. A video there. A moment I wanted to keep. Something about you that made me want to share it.

And eventually, I realized how much of you had quietly found its way into the spaces I used to keep entirely for myself.

Maybe it's because I want people to see you.

Not just because you're beautiful, but because you're someone I'm proud to have in my life. Someone I look at and think, How lucky am I that I get to know this person?

Sometimes I want other people to see the things I see in you. The way you laugh. The way you care. The little things you probably don't even realize are worth remembering. The person you are when no one is asking you to be anything.

And maybe, in some quiet way, I want people to know how lucky I feel to have you—and how lucky I think we both are to have found each other.

You don't have to appear in every sentence for me to know that you're somewhere in the pages.

Sometimes you're the subject. Sometimes you're the reason a thought exists. Sometimes you're the person I imagine reading it. And sometimes, you're simply part of the moment that made me open my laptop and start writing.

Writing about you doesn't just preserve how I feel about you. It preserves who I was while feeling it.

The version of me who was brave enough to ask if I could court you. The version who was still figuring out what it meant to care about someone this deeply. The version who became curious about your dreams, your past, the person you're becoming, and all the parts of you that existed long before I ever came into your life.

Especially that little girl.

I know I can never meet her exactly as she was. I can't go back to the moments that shaped her or change the things she had to experience. But I can meet her through your stories. Through the memories you share. Through the woman she eventually became.

I want to understand her.

I want to know what she dreamed about, what made her happy, what frightened her, what she thought her future would look like. I want to understand how that little girl grew into the woman sitting on the other side of my conversations now.

Maybe someday, you'll read everything I've written here and see more than just letters.

Maybe you'll see a record of how I slowly came to know you.

What I noticed. What I wondered about. What I hoped for. The things I was too shy to say directly but somehow brave enough to write down.

Because this was never supposed to be a love story I wrote alone.

It started as my website.

My thoughts.

My words.

My little corner of the internet.

But then you happened.

And somehow, you became part of the story that was already being written.

Maybe it is still a place for me. Maybe it always will be.

But somewhere between the pages, between the pictures, between the things I wrote and the things I chose to keep, it became a place for both of us, too.

A diary for two.

Not because we planned it that way.

Not because I ever intended for it to happen.

But because some people enter your life so naturally that one day you look around and realize they've become part of everything.

And maybe that's what you became to me.

Not someone I deliberately wrote into the story.

Just someone who slowly became impossible not to write about.

This website doesn't preserve a promise of how our story will end.

It preserves how it felt while we were still becoming.

While you were becoming you.

While I was becoming me.

And somewhere in between, we were becoming us.

posts.title: More Than a Hundred Reasons
posts.subtitle: I could spend a lifetime counting, and I’d still find another reason to love you.
posts.content:
There’s this “100 reasons why I love you” trend that has been lurking around my FYP on TikTok lately. I’ve seen people make their own lists, putting into words a hundred little things they adore about someone. Some write about the way that person smiles, some about their little habits, some about the memories they’ve shared, and some about the things that person probably doesn’t even realize they do. I think there’s something beautiful about it—taking all those little pieces of someone and trying to turn them into words.

But if I were to make one for you, I already know I’d have a problem.

I wouldn’t know where to begin, and I definitely wouldn’t know where to end.

Not because I don’t have enough reasons, but because I have too many. A hundred sounds like a lot until I start thinking about you. Then suddenly, it feels like I’m being asked to choose only a handful of stars from an entire sky and pretend that the rest don’t exist.

I could start with the things that are easy to explain. Your smile. Your laugh. Your voice. The way you tell stories. The way you randomly sing in the middle of a conversation. The little expressions you make without realizing it. The way you get excited when you talk about something you love. The way you can turn the most ordinary story into something I actually want to remember.

But even if I wrote all of those down, I would still be nowhere near finished.

Because there are things about you that I love that don’t really feel like reasons.

They’re feelings.

It’s the comfort of seeing your name appear on my phone. It’s knowing that somewhere in the middle of my day, there might be a message from you. It’s the way an ordinary day can suddenly feel lighter because you decided to tell me something random. It’s the strange happiness I get from being included in the smallest parts of your life.

You can tell me about your day, something that happened at school, something that annoyed you, something that made you laugh, something you’re worried about, something you’re studying, or something completely unrelated that suddenly crossed your mind. And somehow, I want to hear all of it.

I never thought I would become someone who could listen to another person talk for hours and genuinely enjoy it. But then there’s you.

You don’t have to make your stories interesting for me to want to listen. You don’t have to have something important to say. You don’t even have to make sense sometimes. You can simply yap about whatever is on your mind, and I’ll still be there, listening.

Maybe that’s what makes being your listener so easy.

I don’t listen because every story has a lesson.

I listen because it’s you telling it.

And I think there’s a difference.

Maybe that’s also why I stopped minding phone calls.

I used to think phone calls were something I could live without. Then you became the exception. Now, I can find myself enjoying the quietest calls—the ones where you’re studying and I’m doing something else, the ones where you’re reviewing for a demo or return demonstration, the ones where you’re doing your makeup, the ones where you’re telling me about your day, and even the ones where neither of us has anything particularly interesting to say.

Sometimes you’re busy doing your own thing while I’m doing mine.

Sometimes the conversation gets quieter.

Sometimes one of us gets sleepy.

And sometimes we don’t even need to fill the silence.

Just knowing you’re there is enough.

I think those are the moments I would struggle to put into a list.

Because how do I number the comfort of your presence?

How do I make a reason out of the feeling of being able to exist beside someone without having to constantly entertain them?

How do I explain the kind of silence that doesn’t feel awkward because it’s shared with the right person?

Those things don’t feel like reasons anymore.

They feel like home.

And that’s when I realize that maybe I was never supposed to count them in the first place.

“A hundred reasons might be enough for a list, but they could never be enough for you. There are still so many things I have yet to discover, so many moments we have yet to share, and so many reasons I haven’t found yet.”

Because there are still parts of you I haven’t discovered.

There are still conversations we haven’t had, places we haven’t gone to, memories we haven’t made, and versions of ourselves we haven’t met yet. There are still countless ordinary days ahead of us that could become meaningful simply because you were there.

And maybe that’s the part I love most about this.

I don’t know every reason yet.

Some of them haven’t happened.

Some of them are still somewhere in the future, waiting for us.

There might be a future version of you who will give me another reason to smile. Another version of you who will surprise me. Another little habit I’ll eventually notice. Another story you’ll tell me. Another moment where I’ll look at you and think, “There you are. Another reason.”

How could I possibly limit something that hasn’t even finished becoming?

Then there’s the way you care for people.

I admire that part of you more than I probably say. You have this instinct to look after others, to notice when someone needs something, to worry about people, and to make sure they’re okay. And while I know you’re becoming a nurse, I don’t think your ability to care started with the dream of becoming one.

I think it was already part of you long before the uniform, the title, the license, or the hospital.

The profession will give that kindness a name, but the heart behind it was already there.

I’ve watched you continue showing up even when you’re tired. I’ve seen how much you give of yourself even when you have your own things to carry. You somehow find room to care about other people while dealing with your own struggles.

And sometimes, I wish you could see yourself the way I see you.

Maybe then you’d understand why I’m so proud of you.

Not simply because you’re becoming a nurse.

Not because one day people will call you “Nurse.”

But because of the person you are becoming along the way.

I think about the little girl you once were—the girl who had dreams before she knew how difficult it would be to reach them. I never got the chance to meet her, but I still feel a strange tenderness toward that version of you.

Because she became you.

Everything she went through, every difficult day, every moment she had to be strong, every time she kept moving even when she was tired, eventually led to the woman I get to know today.

So when I say I’m rooting for the nurse you’re becoming, I don’t only mean the future version of you in scrubs.

I’m rooting for the little girl who dreamed of becoming her, too.

I’m rooting for every version of you that had to keep going.

And when you finally get to where you’ve been trying so hard to go, I hope you remember the person who started the journey long before she knew where it would lead.

I hope you’re proud of her.

Because I am.

Then there are the little things you’ve unintentionally left behind in my life.

You made me notice pink more than I ever used to.

A color became a reminder of you.

Now, whenever I see something pink, there’s this little part of my mind that immediately thinks of you. It could be something completely insignificant—a shirt, a bag, a sign, something on a shelf, something I pass by without a second thought. And suddenly, I think, “That’s her favorite color.”

It’s funny how someone can change the meaning of something so ordinary.

Before you, it was just a color.

Now, somehow, it carries a piece of you.

And it isn’t only pink.

There are songs that sound different because I associate them with you. There are certain words that mean more because I remember you saying them. There are moments that probably would have disappeared from my memory if you weren’t part of them.

That’s what love seems to do.

It leaves traces.

Little pieces of someone begin appearing in places you never expected them to.

And before you know it, someone has found their way into the smallest corners of your everyday life.

You’ve done that to me.

Without trying.

Without asking.

You’ve simply become part of how I see things.

And I think that’s another reason a hundred could never be enough.

Because I’m not only counting the things you do.

I’m also counting the things you’ve changed in me.

You’ve made me softer in places I didn’t realize were hard. You’ve made me more intentional with the way I love. You’ve taught me that affection doesn’t always have to be loud or grand. Sometimes it’s something as simple as asking if someone has eaten. Sometimes it’s remembering a detail they mentioned weeks ago. Sometimes it’s staying on a call a little longer. Sometimes it’s listening when there’s nothing you can do to fix the problem.

Sometimes love is simply saying, “I’m here.”

And I want to learn how to love you in those little ways.

Not only when everything is beautiful.

Especially when it isn’t.

Because I know there will be days when you come home exhausted. Days when school feels overwhelming. Days when your responsibilities pile up. Days when you question yourself. Days when you feel like you’re not doing enough even though you are.

There will be days when you don’t feel like the strongest version of yourself.

And on those days, I don’t want to be another thing you have to carry.

I want to be someone you can put your burdens down with.

Someone you can tell everything to without worrying that you’re being too much.

Someone who can listen without immediately trying to solve everything.

Someone who can sit beside you in the quiet and let you take your time becoming okay again.

Because loving someone isn’t only about loving the version of them that smiles easily.

Sometimes it means staying when the smile disappears.

Sometimes it means learning their silence.

Sometimes it means being patient with the parts of them that are still trying to understand themselves.

And that’s the kind of love I want to give you.

A love that doesn’t require you to always be happy, strong, productive, or certain.

A love that lets you be human.

You’ll make mistakes.

You’ll have bad days.

You’ll get tired.

You’ll become frustrated.

You’ll change your mind.

There will be moments when you don’t recognize yourself, and there will be days when you feel like you’re falling behind.

But I never want those moments to make you question whether you are still worthy of being loved.

You are.

Even there.

Especially there.

Because if I loved you only for the things you did well, then what would happen on the days when you couldn’t?

If I loved you only because you made me happy, what would happen when life became difficult?

If I loved only the version of you I know today, what would happen when tomorrow changes you?

I don’t want my love for you to be a checklist.

I don’t want to love a collection of qualities and call that loving you.

I want to love the person behind all of them.

And people change.

You will change.

I will change.

The things we want, the things we fear, the things we believe, and the way we see the world will continue changing as we grow.

So maybe I don’t want to write down one hundred reasons.

Maybe I want to leave room for the one hundred and first.

And the one hundred and second.

And the five hundredth.

And every reason that doesn’t exist yet because we haven’t lived the moment that will create it.

There are still so many versions of you I haven’t met.

The future you.

The older you.

The you who finally reaches the dreams you’ve been working toward.

The you who becomes more confident.

The you who learns that resting doesn’t mean failing.

The you who looks back at who you are today and realizes just how far you’ve come.

I want to meet all of them.

And I hope that, through every version, I’ll still find something new to love.

Maybe someday, we’ll look back at who we are now and laugh at the things we used to worry about. Maybe we’ll remember these late-night conversations, the random calls, the stories that didn’t really have a point, the little things we thought were ordinary, and realize that those were the moments that quietly became some of our favorites.

Maybe there will be memories we haven’t even imagined yet.

And maybe some of those memories will become reasons I never thought to write down today.

That’s why I could never promise you only a hundred.

I’d rather promise you that I’ll keep noticing.

I’ll keep paying attention to the little things.

I’ll keep learning you.

I’ll keep discovering the parts of you that you haven’t shown me yet.

I’ll keep finding beauty in the ordinary things you do.

And when I think I’ve already found every possible reason, I’ll probably find another one the next day.

I might start a list someday.

I might write the first few reasons.

I might even reach one hundred.

But I know myself well enough to know that when I reach the hundredth one, I’ll probably stare at the page and think, “Wait. I forgot this.”

And then I’ll add another.

Then another.

Then another.

Until the list stops looking like a list and starts looking like a lifetime.

Because maybe that’s what I actually want.

Not a hundred reasons.

A lifetime of reasons.

A lifetime of getting to know you, listening to your stories, laughing at your randomness, supporting your dreams, being there through the difficult days, celebrating the good ones, and meeting every version of you that life allows me to know.

So no, I don’t think I’ll join the “100 reasons why I love you” trend.

One hundred is beautiful.

But one hundred is still a limit.

And I don’t want to put a limit on you.

I don’t want to reach a number and say, “That’s everything.”

Because it isn’t.

There will always be something else.

Another memory.

Another conversation.

Another laugh.

Another ordinary day that somehow becomes special because you were in it.

Another little thing you do without realizing it.

Another reason I didn’t know yesterday.

Another reason I’ll discover tomorrow.

And maybe, after all this time, that will always be my favorite thing about loving you: there will never be an ending to discover.

So if you ever ask me how many reasons I have for loving you, I might never be able to give you an exact number.

I’ll probably just tell you that I stopped counting.

Not because I ran out.

But because there were too many.

Because you became more than a list could hold, more than a number could measure, and more than a hundred reasons could ever explain.

I could spend forever trying to name every reason.

And I think I’d still be writing when forever ends.

posts.title: Someone You Never Expected
posts.subtitle: Yet somehow, I became the answer to a prayer you never knew you made.
posts.content:
I didn't know this is what it feels like to become someone's answered prayer.

You’ve told me so many times that I’ve become an answered prayer for you, and every time you say it, I still don't know exactly how to respond. I can't fully explain this roller-coaster of emotions that comes over me whenever I hear those words from you. There’s happiness, disbelief, warmth, and a kind of gratitude that I don't even know how to put into words.

But yes, I love hearing it from you.

I love hearing you say that I've become an answered prayer for you. I don't think I'll ever get tired of hearing it, no matter how many times you tell me. You could tell me tomorrow, the next day, and a hundred more times after that, and I'd probably still smile the same way.

Because there's something so beautiful about knowing that my presence in your life means that much to you.

I've always thought of answered prayers as something grand—something you've waited years for, something you've asked the universe for in the quietest moments, something that arrives when you least expect it. I never imagined that an answered prayer could be a person. Someone you meet on an ordinary night. Someone you slowly get attached to through conversations, laughter, late-night calls, random stories, and all the little moments that didn't seem significant at first.

And somehow, that person became me.

I don't know what I did to deserve being called someone's answered prayer. I don't know if I can ever fully understand what you saw in me that made you feel that way. But I know one thing: I will never take those words lightly.

Because if I am an answered prayer to you, then you should know that you became something I never knew I was praying for, too.

Maybe I just didn't know how to name it before you came along.

I didn't know I was looking for someone whose voice would become my comfort. I didn't know I needed someone I could talk to until midnight about everything and nothing. I didn't know I would care about someone's day so much that I'd want to hear every little detail, even the parts you think aren't worth telling. I didn't know I'd find myself remembering your favorite color, your little habits, your random stories, and all the tiny things that make you who you are.

I didn't know I was waiting for you.

And maybe that's why hearing you call me your answered prayer means so much.

Because while you tell me that I am something you prayed for, I'm slowly realizing that you have become something I would be afraid to lose.

So no, I don't care how many times you tell me.

Tell me again.

Tell me when you're happy.

Tell me when we're laughing.

Tell me during one of our random late-night conversations.

Tell me when you're tired and we barely have anything to talk about.

Tell me even when you think I've already heard it too many times.

I will still listen.

I will still smile.

And somewhere inside me, I'll still think about how incredibly lucky I am that someone like you looks at me and sees an answered prayer.

Maybe I'll never find the perfect words to explain what that feels like.

But perhaps I don't need to.

Because whenever you tell me, I think my heart already knows how to answer.

I love that.

I love knowing that I became something good in your life.

I love knowing that my existence could bring you comfort.

I love knowing that somewhere between an ordinary midnight and all the conversations that followed, I became someone you once prayed for.

And more than anything—

I love you.

Maybe that's the simplest answer I can give.

You call me your answered prayer, but I hope you know that loving you feels like an answered prayer I never knew I had.

posts.title: What Could Possibly Come After Ten?
posts.subtitle: Maybe there was never supposed to be a “but” when it comes to you.
posts.content:
Do you know the “10/10” trend? The “She's a 10, but…” one? For sure, you've probably thought about it yourself at some point—like, “I'm a 10, but I can't cook a proper meal.” Hahahaha, just kidding. I honestly don't care whether you can cook or not. You could burn the kitchen trying to make eggs, and I'd probably still give you a 10.

Because for me, you're a complete 10 out of 10.

No but.

You're a 10 because you take care of other people. You make sure everyone is okay, and somehow, you even find a way to take care of me despite having your own battles to fight. You never fail to check up on me, and you do the same for the people around you. You don't do it simply because you're becoming a nurse. You do it because caring comes naturally to you. It's one of the ways you show your love—quietly, sincerely, and without expecting anything in return. You notice when someone isn't okay. You remember the little things. You ask if someone has eaten, if they've arrived safely, and if they're doing fine. You have this way of making people feel cared for without even realizing how much those little gestures mean. And I hope you know that I notice them, too.

You're a 10 because you still show up even when you're busy and tired, as if you're not carrying battles of your own. You have your own deadlines, responsibilities, exhaustion, and moments when you probably just want to lie down and forget about everything for a while, yet somehow, you still make time for the people you love. You still reply, you still call, you still ask how my day went, and you still listen to my random stories. Even when you're exhausted, you somehow make me feel like I deserve a little piece of your time. I don't take that for granted. I know your time is precious, especially when you already have so much on your plate, and the fact that you choose to share even a little of it with me means more than you probably realize.

You're a 10 because you have such a soft heart, and I know I should take care of it as if it were something precious—because it is. I know the world can be harsh, and I know you've experienced moments that could have made you colder, yet somehow, you still choose to care. You still choose to be gentle. You still choose to love people despite knowing that loving someone can sometimes hurt. And that softness of yours is something I never want to take advantage of. I want to protect it, not change it. I want to be someone who makes you feel safe enough to keep being soft, even when the world gives you reasons not to be.

You're a 10 because you make people feel seen. You have this way of making someone feel like their presence matters, whether they're telling you something important or simply rambling about the most random thing. You listen, you remember, and you respond in a way that makes people feel like they're worth your attention. I know there are probably moments when you don't realize you're doing it, but I've noticed how naturally you make people feel heard. And maybe that's one of the things I admire most about you—you don't need grand gestures to make someone feel important. Sometimes, simply being there is already enough.

You're a 10 because you let yourself be yourself around me. You don't always have to be composed, serious, or the strong person everyone expects you to be. You can be loud, quiet, silly, dramatic, sleepy, clingy, or completely random. You can yap about something for an hour without realizing how much time has passed, randomly sing during our calls, complain about your day, tell me a story that has absolutely no ending, or simply stay quiet while we do our own things. And I love that I get to see those sides of you. I don't want only the polished version of you. I want the real you—the one who doesn't have to pretend around me.

You're a 10 because you're human. You get tired. You make mistakes. You overthink. You have bad days. Sometimes you don't know what you're doing, and sometimes you question whether you're doing enough. You don't always have everything figured out, and you don't have to. I don't love you because I think you're perfect. I love you because you're you, and somehow, even the imperfect parts of you have become things I wouldn't want to erase. Your flaws don't make you less deserving of love. They simply make you human, and I want to love you as a whole person, not just the parts that are easy to love.

You're a 10 because you keep trying. Even when things don't go the way you planned, you still find a way to move forward. Even when you're exhausted, you still get up and continue. Even when you doubt yourself, there's still a part of you that refuses to give up on the life you're trying to build. I know there are days when everything feels overwhelming, but I hope you know that I see your effort. I see how hard you're trying, even when you think nobody notices. And I'll always be proud of you for choosing to continue, especially on the days when continuing is the hardest thing to do.

You're a 10 because of the girl you used to be, the woman you are now, and the nurse you're slowly becoming. I know how much you've worked for that dream, and I know becoming the person you want to be isn't always easy. There will be exhausting duties, sleepless nights, difficult examinations, return demonstrations, mistakes, and moments when you'll wonder whether you're really capable of becoming the nurse you dreamed of being. But I hope you never forget how far you've already come. I see the little girl who once had a dream, the girl who kept going despite everything, and the woman who is now slowly turning that dream into reality. And when the day finally comes when someone calls you “Nurse,” I'll be one of the people quietly smiling and thinking about every difficult day that brought you there.

You're a 10 because you make ordinary things feel special. A random phone call, a late-night conversation, a simple “have you eaten?”, a message telling me about your day, a picture of something pink because you know it's your favorite color, a random song, or even just a few minutes of your time—somehow, you've made these little things mean so much to me. You don't have to do anything extraordinary to make me happy. Sometimes, your presence alone is enough. That's what I love about us. We can be doing absolutely nothing, and somehow, I still feel like I'm exactly where I want to be.

You're a 10 because you've become my comfort person. You're the person I look for when I have something I want to share, the person I want to hear from at the end of the day, and the person whose name can instantly make me smile. Somewhere along the way, talking to you became something I look forward to, and hearing your voice became one of my favorite parts of the day. I never thought I'd be someone who enjoyed phone calls this much, but then again, maybe phone calls were never the problem. Maybe I just needed the right person on the other end of the line.

You're a 10 because you make me want to become softer, too. Loving you has taught me that love doesn't always have to be loud or grand. Sometimes, it is simply listening to your stories, remembering the things you casually mention, checking if you've eaten, reminding you to rest, waiting until you get home safely, and being there when you need someone. You make me want to love intentionally—to make sure that the person I love never has to question whether she is loved. And if I can give you even a fraction of the comfort and happiness you've given me, then I'll consider myself lucky.

You're a 10 because you're someone I can admire without putting you on a pedestal. I don't need to pretend you're perfect to know how special you are. I can see your struggles, your tired days, your insecurities, your mistakes, and the parts of yourself you might not always like, and somehow, none of those things make me love you less. If anything, they make me want to understand you more. Because loving someone isn't about loving only their brightest days. It's about staying gentle with them when the light isn't as bright.

And maybe that's why, if someone asks me, “She's a 10, but…”, I'd probably interrupt them before they could even finish.

Because what but?

What could I possibly add after 10?

You're a 10 when you're happy, a 10 when you're tired, a 10 when you're dressed up, and a 10 when you're still doing your makeup. You're a 10 when you're studying, when you're complaining about your duties, when you're sleepy, when you're being dramatic, when you're yapping, and even when you're quiet. You're a 10 when you feel confident, and you're still a 10 when you're struggling to see anything good about yourself.

Your worth doesn't decrease just because you have a bad day.

So maybe the trend asks, “She's a 10, but…”

But I'd rather change the question.

She's a 10.

And that's it.

No but.

No exceptions.

No conditions.

No need to prove anything.

Just you.

And if I had to rate how much I love you?

10 out of 10 wouldn't even come close.

And maybe that's why I could never put a limit on how much I can love you. Every day, you give me another reason to admire you, another little thing to appreciate, and another side of you that makes me think, how did I get so lucky to know someone like you? I don't think I'll ever run out of reasons to love you, because the more I know you, the more I see how much there is to love.

You're not a 10 because you're perfect. You're a 10 because even in the moments when you don't feel like one, I'll still see everything that makes you worth loving.

So if the question is, “She's a 10, but…”—I don't think I could ever finish that sentence.

Because there is no but.

There is just you.

And somehow, that's more than enough for me.

posts.title: What If Knowing You More Only Makes Me Love You More?
posts.subtitle: Maybe every new piece of you I discover is just another reason to fall.
posts.content:
I keep seeing the phrase, “Does knowing me more lead to loving me less?”  And I remember that I even wrote something related to it before, but back then, it was all about me. This time, I want to rephrase it and make it about you. Maybe it should be, “Knowing you more could never make me love you less.” Or perhaps, “Knowing you more will never lead me to love you less.”

You see, my love, it's just a single phrase, but there is such a huge meaning behind it.

Because for me, knowing you more isn't simply knowing your favorite color, your favorite food, the songs you listen to, or the little things that make you smile. It's knowing who you are and who you're becoming. It's learning the person behind the things you show everyone else. It's understanding the parts of you that you don't always talk about. It's learning what makes you happy, what makes you uncomfortable, what makes you feel safe, what makes you anxious, what you need when you're tired, what you want when you're dreaming, and what you need from someone when life becomes too heavy.

It's almost like studying you—not in a way that makes you something to be analyzed, but in a way that makes me want to understand every little piece of you.

Your wants.

Your needs.

Your favorites.

Your dislikes.

Your habits.

Your little quirks.

The things that make you laugh.

The things that make you quiet.

The things you get excited about.

The things you overthink.

The dreams you're chasing.

The fears you don't always say out loud.

Even the little things you probably don't think anyone notices.

I want to know them.

Not because I want to memorize you like a list of facts, but because I want to understand how to love you better.

I want to know what kind of comfort you need when you've had a difficult day. I want to know when you need someone to listen and when you simply need someone to stay beside you. I want to know the difference between your “I'm okay” that genuinely means you're okay and your “I'm okay” that secretly means you don't want to talk about it yet.

I want to know the things that make you feel loved, not just the things that make you feel noticed.

And the more I know, the more I realize that knowing someone doesn't make them less lovable.

It makes them more human.

And somehow, that makes me love you even more.

Because I don't want to love some perfect version of you that exists only in my imagination. I want to love the real you—the person who gets tired, gets frustrated, makes mistakes, changes her mind, has bad days, overthinks sometimes, laughs at the most random things, and still continues to become the person she's meant to be.

I want to know you beyond the version of yourself that is easiest to love.

I want to know you completely, or at least as completely as you are willing to let me.

And in the end, after knowing you more, I know one thing for certain:

I will never, ever love you less.

Because, like I said in one of my previous letters, if I love, I love more.

And loving you feels like you've already become my other half—not because I believe I am incomplete without you, but because somehow, you've become a part of my life that I cannot imagine simply removing from it.

You've become part of my ordinary days.

Part of my thoughts.

Part of my little routines.

Part of the things I look forward to.

Part of the stories I want to tell.

Part of the person I think about when something makes me smile.

And somewhere along the way, you've become someone I don't want to lose.

Not because I want to hold you so tightly that you can't be yourself, but because I value the person you are and the place you've found in my life.

I want you to grow.

I want you to change.

I want you to discover new things about yourself.

I want you to become someone you've never imagined you could be.

And when you do, I want to know that version of you, too.

Because loving you doesn't mean loving only who you are today.

It means being willing to meet all the versions of you that tomorrow brings.

So think about that phrase again:

“Does knowing me more lead to loving me less? ”

Now turn it around.

Does knowing you more lead me to loving you less?

No.

Not even close.

If anything, every new thing I learn about you gives me another reason to stay curious, another reason to appreciate you, another reason to fall a little deeper.

So, do I think knowing you more is enough?

No.

I don't think I'll ever feel like I've known enough.

Because there will always be another story I haven't heard, another dream you haven't told me about, another little habit I haven't noticed yet, another part of your heart you haven't shown me.

And I want to discover them.

Slowly.

Gently.

Without rushing you.

I would like—no, I mean, I would love—to know you more.

And if knowing you more means I get to love you more, then let me keep learning.

Let me keep listening.

Let me keep discovering.

Let me keep falling.

Because I don't want to reach a point where I can say, “I already know everything about you.”

I want to reach a point where, even after years of knowing you, I can still look at you and think:

“There is still so much of you left for me to love.”

And maybe that's the real difference.

I don't want to know you more so I can decide whether you're worth loving.

I want to know you more because I already know you're worth loving—and I want to discover every reason why.

posts.title: Does Every “I Love You” Have a Different Meaning?
posts.subtitle: Because sometimes three words can carry an entire heart.
posts.content:
I love you.

I love you so much.

I love you more.

Is there really any difference between those three?

Maybe there is.

Maybe there isn't.

But to me, those three words aren't just words. They carry different feelings, different depths, and different ways of saying what my heart sometimes struggles to explain. To some people, “I love you” might be nothing more than a phrase they say out of habit. Some people say it so easily, as if those words don't hold any weight. As if they're just three ordinary words that can be said whenever the moment feels right.

But I don't see them that way.

When I tell you “I love you,” I mean it.

I mean that I choose you.

I mean that I care about the little things you tell me, even the things you think are insignificant. I mean that your happiness matters to me. I mean that your bad days matter, too. I mean that I want to know how your day went, whether it was the best day you've had or one you'd rather forget.

When I tell you “I love you so much,” it's because sometimes “I love you” doesn't feel big enough to contain everything I feel for you.

It's the love that grows in the middle of ordinary conversations.

It's the love I feel when I hear your voice.

It's the love behind every late-night call, every random message, every little thing that reminds me of you.

It's the love that makes me smile when I see your name on my screen.

It's the love that makes me remember your favorite color.

It's the love that makes me want to write another letter even when I've already written so many.

And then there's “I love you more.”

Maybe you think I'm simply trying to win an argument whenever I say it.

Maybe it's just our little way of teasing each other.

But sometimes, when I say “I love you more,” I don't mean more than you love me.

I mean that I want to keep finding more ways to love you.

More patience.

More understanding.

More effort.

More reassurance.

More time.

More little things that make you feel cared for.

More reasons for you to never question whether you're loved.

Because for me, loving you isn't supposed to be a competition where one of us has to prove that we love the other more.

It's not about keeping score.

It's not about who said it first or who said it last.

It's simply about giving love freely and letting it grow.

And maybe that's the difference between those three.

"I love you" is me telling you how I feel.

"I love you so much" is me trying to tell you that my feelings are bigger than the words can hold.

And "I love you more" is my promise that I don't want my love for you to remain exactly where it is. I want it to grow with us.

I want to love you more gently when you're tired.

More patiently when we're struggling to understand each other.

More intentionally when life gets busy.

More loudly when you need reassurance.

And more quietly when you don't need words at all.

Because I don't want “I love you” to become something you hear so often that it loses its meaning.

I want you to feel it.

I want you to see it in the way I treat you.

I want you to hear it in the way I listen.

I want you to find it in the little things I remember.

I want you to recognize it in the way I stay.

Because anyone can say “I love you.”

But I want my actions to make you believe it.

I want my love to be something you can rest in, not something you constantly have to question.

So if I tell you “I love you” a hundred times, I hope you never think I'm simply repeating myself.

I'm reminding you.

I'm reminding you that you are loved today.

And tomorrow.

And on the days when you're happy.

And on the days when you're tired.

And on the days when you don't feel particularly lovable.

Especially then.

So maybe there isn't really a difference between “I love you,” “I love you so much,” and “I love you more.”

Maybe they're simply different ways of saying the same thing:

I love you, and I mean it every single time.

And if words ever become insufficient, I'll find another way to tell you.

I'll write it.

I'll show it.

I'll stay.

I'll choose you.

And I'll keep finding new ways to say those three little words until you never have to wonder what they mean when they come from me.

posts.title: Will Always Be a Shelter, Never a Storm
posts.subtitle: I cannot promise a life without storms, but I can promise not to become one.
posts.content:
The Ridleys said, “I'll be more of a shelter and less of a storm.” And in this world full of doubts, pressure, stress, and noise—where gentleness sometimes feels so rare—let me remind you that I'll be your shelter. Let me be your pahinga. Let me be the person you can come home to when the world becomes too loud. Let me be your comfort person, the one you can run to when you don't know where else to go.

I don't want to be another source of heaviness in your life. There are already enough things outside our control that make life difficult. There are already enough expectations, responsibilities, worries, and days that leave us exhausted. So when you come to me, I want you to feel like you can finally put everything down, even just for a while.

You don't have to be strong with me.

You don't have to pretend that you're okay.

You don't have to carefully choose your words because you're afraid I'll misunderstand you.

You can tell me what you're feeling. You can tell me what hurt you. You can tell me when you're angry, when you're tired, when you're scared, or when you simply don't know what you're feeling at all.

I want to know you in those moments, too.

And I promise that someday, when we have a home of our own, I don't want it to be filled with storms. I don't want our home to become another place where you have to walk on eggshells, afraid that one wrong word will turn into an argument. I don't want shouting to become our language, or blame to become our way of solving things.

I want our home to be a shelter.

A place where you can breathe.

A place where you can express yourself without fear of being judged.

A place where you can be completely yourself without worrying that you'll become too much.

A place where we can talk about things even when they're difficult, where we choose understanding before anger, and where we learn how to meet each other halfway instead of trying to prove who's right.

And when we do hurt each other—because I know that loving someone doesn't mean we'll never make mistakes—I hope we remember that we're on the same side.

I don't want us to fight against each other.

I want us to fight for each other.

I want us to learn how to apologize without pride getting in the way. I want us to learn how to listen without immediately preparing a defense. I want us to be able to say, “That hurt me,” without turning it into an accusation and “I'm sorry,” without feeling like we've lost something by admitting we were wrong.

Because love shouldn't feel like a battlefield.

It should feel like coming home.

And if one day you come home after the hardest day you've had and all you want is silence, I'll sit beside you in silence. If you want to talk, I'll listen. If you want to cry, I'll hold you. If you need space, I'll give you space without making you feel like you're being abandoned.

I want to learn the difference between when you need my words and when you simply need my presence.

I want to be the person who knows when to say something and when to just stay.

Because I don't want to promise you a life without storms. I know I can't control everything that happens outside our home. There will still be difficult days. There will still be problems we can't immediately solve. There will be moments when we're both tired, frustrated, or overwhelmed.

But I can promise you this:

I don't want to become the storm you have to escape from. I want to be the place you can escape to.

I want our home to be filled with laughter, sleepy conversations, random stories, quiet mornings, late-night talks, and the kind of silence that doesn't need to be explained.

I want there to be a place where you can leave your worries at the door.

Where your tiredness is allowed to exist.

Where your dreams are encouraged.

Where your mistakes are forgiven.

Where your feelings have a place.

Where your voice is heard.

Where your heart is safe.

And maybe someday, when you look around that home, you'll realize that we built something neither of us had to be afraid of.

Something gentle.

Something warm.

Something that feels like us.

So until that day comes, let me start with the little things.

Let me listen when you need to rant.

Let me hold you when you're tired.

Let me remind you to rest when you've forgotten that you're allowed to.

Let me celebrate your victories, no matter how small.

Let me sit beside you through the days that don't go according to plan.

Let me be your pahinga after a long day.

And when the world becomes too much, come home to me.

Not necessarily to a place.

Not yet.

But to me.

Because if I get the privilege of loving you, I want you to know that you will never have to wonder whether there is a soft place for you to land.

There will always be a place for you here.

And if the world insists on being a storm, then let me spend my life learning how to be your shelter.

posts.title: 7 Ways To Take Care of Nature (Life)
posts.content:
Nature mirrors our own journey. It teaches us that just as life demands care, patience, and respect, so too does the world around us. The steps we take to protect nature are the same steps we must take to nurture our own lives.

1. WE MUST OBSERVE.

Observation in nature means listening to the wind, feeling the sun’s warmth, noticing the quiet strength of trees. In life, it means being mindful— understanding our emotions, recognizing our needs, and paying attention to the people around us. Without observation, we move blindly through existence. By observing fully, we live more fully, embracing each moment with curiosity, compassion, and wonder.


2. WE MUST PRESERVE.

We protect the rivers and forests because they sustain us—likewise, we must protect our dreams, our peace, and our relationships. What is valuable must be guarded with intention, whether it is a delicate flower or a fragile hope. Just as nature's beauty and resources require care and protection, our inner worlds—dreams, peace, and relationships—need nurturing and safeguarding. By tending to these precious aspects of life with the same dedication we give to preserving the environment, we create a foundation for growth, resilience, and lasting fulfillment. Protecting what matters most is an act of self-love and foresight, ensuring that the things that bring us joy and meaning are preserved for generations to come.

3. WE MUST REDUCE.

Nature reminds us that too much of anything—pollution, waste, greed—leads to destruction. In life, we must lessen negativity, anger, and unnecessary burdens. By letting go of what weighs us down, we create space to grow, to heal, to breathe. Letting go of toxic thoughts, harmful relationships, and self-imposed limitations creates room for growth, healing, and renewal. In this way, we restore harmony within ourselves and with the world around us, fostering a life of clarity, purpose, and peace.

4. WE MUST NURTURE. 

Nurturing brings life to bloom—water nourishes seeds, shelter safeguards the vulnerable, and space allows the wild to thrive. while nurturing in life means uplifting one another through kindness, fostering growth with patience, and creating spaces where potential can unfold. Without nurturing, possibilities fade, and the beauty of growth remains unrealized. In this way, nurturing becomes a catalyst for transformation, unlocking the beauty and potential that lies within every individual and community.

5. WE MUST REFLECT. 

Reflection is seen in the calm waters that mirror the sky, in the quiet moments after a storm, and in the stillness of a winter's night. while in life means taking the time to look inward, to learn from our experiences, and to understand the journey we've traveled. Without reflection, we move forward without wisdom, repeating the mistakes of the past. By embracing stillness and introspection, we gain clarity on our path, learn from our triumphs and setbacks, and make informed choices for the future. Through reflection, we honor our journey and prepare ourselves to walk forward with greater insight and purpose.

6. WE MUST EDUCATE. 

Just as we teach others how to care for the earth, we must also share wisdom about life—lessons of kindness, resilience, and humility. Teaching strengthens not just the learner but also the teacher— it roots our values deeper into our being. Teaching and mentoring not only guide others but also deepen our understanding and commitment to these values. By passing on what we've learned, we reinforce our own principles and contribute to a more compassionate and thoughtful world.


7. WE MUST ACT WITH LOVE.

Nature thrives on gentle stewardship, and so do our souls. to live with love— choosing compassion over judgment, gratitude over entitlement— builds a life that is rich and meaningful. love is the quiet revolution that changes both the earth and the human heart. Love is the quiet force that nurtures both the earth and the soul. When we approach life with compassion, gratitude, and humility, we create ripples of positive change. This gentle stewardship of our hearts and the world around us fosters harmony, resilience, and beauty, reminding us that love is the greatest revolution of all.


Taking care of nature is not separate from taking care of life—it is life. As we protect the forests, the seas, and the skies, we are also learning to protect the fragile, beautiful journey within ourselves.
