posts.title: Am I Asking You the Right Way?
posts.subtitle: Sometimes, the hardest thing to ask is for permission to love someone properly.
posts.content:
It's funny how easily I show my love to you. Maybe it's because I've never known how to love halfway. Maybe it's because I don't believe in giving someone I love the bare minimum. Or maybe this is simply the way I know how to love you—with everything I have, without holding myself back.

I want you to feel it in the little things I do, in the words I write, in the time I give you, and in every little reminder that you are loved. I want you to feel it so deeply that you never have to doubt yourself, question yourself, or wonder whether you are worthy of all the love I give you.

Because you are, my love.

You are more than worthy of everything.

I never want you to feel like you have to earn my affection. I don't want you to wonder if you're being too much, if you're asking for too much, or if there's a limit to how much love you deserve. There isn't. At least not from me.

I never settle for less, and I never love less. If I love, I love more.

More than yesterday.

More than I thought I could.

More than I know how to put into words.

And even though I've been courting you—or at least, I think I have—am I already? I haven't even properly asked you. So, can I?

Can I have your permission to court you?

Can I intentionally pursue you, not because I want to rush whatever this is between us, but because I want to take my time getting to know you even more? Can I continue showing you how much you mean to me, without expecting anything from you before you're ready to give it?

If you let me, I won't promise to be the perfect suitor to you. I don't think I could ever make that promise because I'm still learning, still figuring out how to love you in the ways you deserve. But I can promise that I'll always try. I'll give you the best of what I can—not because I expect perfection from you in return, but because you are someone worth making an effort for.

I'll learn your little habits. I'll remember the things you casually mention. I'll listen to the stories you've already told me a hundred times. I'll celebrate your smallest victories and stay beside you through the days that don't feel like victories at all.

I won't promise that I'll always know what to say.

But I'll promise to listen.

I won't promise that I'll always know how to fix things.

But I'll promise to stay.

And I won't promise that I'll never make mistakes.

But I will promise that when I do, I'll acknowledge them, learn from them, and try to do better.

Because if you give me the chance to court you, I don't want to simply impress you.

I want to know you.

I want to understand you.

I want to love you intentionally.

Every word I've written, every little thing I've done, every time I've stayed up just to talk to you, every time I've listened to you tell me about your day—none of it was something I did simply because I wanted to impress you.

I did it because it's you.

I know you know that.

I know you can feel how much I love you, even in the things I don't explicitly say. I know you can probably see it in the way I remember the smallest things about you, in the way I get excited when I see something that reminds me of you, in the way I listen to your stories even when they have no ending, and in the way I always seem to find another reason to stay a little longer whenever we're together.

I told you before—this is one of the ways I court you.

I write you letters.

I put my feelings into words because sometimes saying "I love you" doesn't feel like enough. Sometimes three words can't hold everything I want you to know.

So I write.

I write about the way you make me feel. I write about the things I notice about you. I write about your voice, your laughter, your stories, your little habits, your favorite color, your dreams, your tired days, and all the little pieces of you that somehow became important to me.

I know writing letters might seem like the bare minimum.

Maybe it is.

But if writing you one letter makes you feel loved for a moment, then I'd rather write you hundreds.

Thousands, even.

I'll fill pages with you if that's what it takes to remind you how much you mean to me.

I'll write about you on the days when you're happy and on the days when you're exhausted. I'll write when you accomplish something you've been working toward, and I'll write when you feel like you haven't accomplished enough. I'll write when you need reassurance, when you need someone to remind you that you're doing well, and even when you simply need to be reminded that someone is proud of you.

Because I don't want my love to exist only in the moments when everything is easy.

I want you to feel it in the ordinary days, too.

In the random messages.

In the late-night calls.

In the "have you eaten?" texts.

In the "get home safe."

In the "I'm proud of you."

In the little things that may seem insignificant but quietly say, I'm thinking about you.

Maybe that's what I mean when I say I don't know how to love less.

I don't know how to look at someone I love and decide that they only deserve a certain amount of affection. I don't know how to count the times I've said "I love you" or keep track of how much effort I've given. I don't want to love you like I'm keeping score.

I just want to love you.

And if someday you forget how worthy you are, I'll remind you.

If you ever question whether you're enough, I'll remind you.

If you ever wonder whether you're lovable on the days when you're tired, messy, overwhelmed, or unsure of yourself, I'll remind you.

You don't have to be the best version of yourself for me to love you.

You don't have to have everything figured out.

You don't have to be perfect.

You just have to be you.

And somehow, that's always been more than enough for me.

So yes, I'm still courting you.

I'm still trying to make you fall for me.

I'm still writing letters and finding little ways to make you smile.

But somewhere along the way, I think these letters stopped being only about making you mine.

They became my way of saying:

I see you.

I appreciate you.

I'm proud of you.

I'm here.

And most importantly—

You are loved.

Maybe one day, when you look back at all these letters, you'll realize that I wasn't simply trying to win your heart.

I was trying to show you what it feels like to be loved without having to question whether you deserve it.

I want you to look at my love and never feel like you have to compete for it. I want you to feel safe enough to be yourself around me. I want you to know that you can be soft, loud, tired, emotional, excited, messy, or completely unsure of yourself, and I will still see you as someone worth loving.

And if I have to write a thousand more letters just to make you believe that, then I'll gladly write every single one.

Because if loving you means filling pages with everything my heart has been trying to say, then give me all the paper in the world.

I'll write until I run out of pages.

And if I somehow run out of words, I'll find another way to show you.

I'll never run out of reasons to write about you.

I'll never run out of things to love about you.

And I'll never want to love you any less.

Because if you let me, I don't just want to be someone who once courted you.

I want to be someone who, even years from now, still finds new reasons to choose you.

posts.title: It's My Someone's Favorite Color
posts.subtitle: If I can't carry you everywhere, I'll carry little pieces of you instead.
posts.content:
Many people thought my favorite color was pink. They thought it was my branding, my signature color—that's why some of them would gift me something pink. They'd see anything pink and immediately think of me. But no one knows, not even my parents, that my actual favorite color is blue.

The reason I have so many pink things, whether they're inside or outside my bag—keychains, phone cases, little accessories, and even the smallest things I carry with me—is that pink is someone's favorite color.

Someone I can call mine.

Someone who became my comfort person.

Someone whose own little branding is the color pink.

The moment I found out that pink was your favorite color, I don't think you realized how much that tiny piece of information stayed with me. It was such a simple thing to know about you, but somehow, it became something I started carrying with me everywhere. I began putting little pieces of pink into my own things—not because pink suddenly became my favorite color, but because I wanted to have something that reminded me of you.

Maybe it sounds silly.

It's just a color.

But sometimes, the smallest things become meaningful when they're connected to someone you love.

Every pink keychain I put on my bag, every pink phone case I chose, every little pink thing I decided to keep became a quiet way of keeping you close. It felt like carrying a tiny piece of you wherever I went. I didn't need a photograph or a reminder written somewhere. Sometimes, all I needed was to see that familiar color, and suddenly, you were the first person that came to mind.

And whenever I see something pink, my first instinct is still to message you.

"Look, it's your favorite color."

Or sometimes, I don't even have anything else to say.

"It's pink."

As if you don't already know.

As if I don't already know.

But somehow, I still want to tell you.

Because I love sharing little things with you. Even the most ordinary moments feel a little more special when I can turn them into something that reminds me of you. I could be walking somewhere and suddenly notice a pink flower, a pink sign, a pink bag, or some random pink object sitting on a shelf, and before I even realize it, I've already thought of you.

It's funny how a color can become a person.

How something that used to be nothing more than a shade can suddenly carry someone's laugh, their voice, their stories, and their presence.

Pink became you to me.

And maybe that's why I never correct people when they assume it's my favorite color. I just smile and let them believe it. I don't really mind if they think pink is part of who I am.

Because in a way, they're not entirely wrong.

Pink did become a part of me.

Just not because I chose it for myself.

I chose it because it reminds me of you.

Blue may be the color I've always loved, but pink became the color I learned to love because of someone else. And there's something strangely beautiful about that—the fact that loving someone can make you find meaning in something you never thought would mean anything to you.

So maybe pink isn't my favorite color.

Maybe it's just your color that I get to carry with me.

And whenever I see it, I'll probably still think of you.

I'll still want to send you a picture.

I'll still want to say, "Look, it's your favorite color."

Because somewhere along the way, I stopped seeing pink as just pink.

I started seeing you.

posts.title: The Art of Matcha
posts.content:
As I prepare matcha, I'm reminded that every step is a gesture of love. The ritual becomes a meditation, a way to slow down and appreciate the beauty in the everyday. With each whisk, I feel a sense of care and intention, like I'm nurturing a relationship.


¹ CHOOSING THE RIGHT MATCHA

I look for high-quality matcha powder with a rich, grassy aroma and vibrant green color. The better the matcha, the more nuanced the flavors, and the more joy I find in the process. It's like selecting a special someone to share a moment with— the right match makes all the difference. The vibrant green color is like a burst of freshness, a symbol of the tea's vitality and energy. With the right matcha, every sip is a celebration of flavor, a moment of tranquility, and a connection to the simple joys of life. The nuances of the tea unfold like a story, rich and multifaceted, leaving me grateful for the experience.


² PREPARING THE LOVE

As I sift the matcha powder, I'm gentle, mindful of the delicate leaves. Adding hot water, I watch the tea unfurl its flavors, releasing the subtle bitterness and umami notes. The process is calming, like a warm hug on a chilly day. The steam rises, carrying the aroma of the matcha, a delicate balance of grassy and vegetal notes. As I wait for the perfect moment to whisk, the tea seems to awaken, its flavors mingling and deepening. With each step, I feel more grounded, more present, as if the ritual of preparing matcha is a bridge between the chaos of the world and the tranquility of the moment. The calmness spreads, like the warmth of a cup held in cold hands, comforting and reassuring.


³ THE WHISKING TECHNIQUE 

I whisk the matcha with a gentle, zig-zag motion, feeling the bamboo whisk dance across the bowl. The smooth, frothy texture that forms is like the comfort of a loved one's touch— soothing and reassuring. With each stroke, the matcha transforms, its vibrant green hue deepening, its flavors unfolding like the petals of a flower. The froth that forms is like the gentle caress of a summer breeze, light and airy, carrying the essence of serenity. In this moment, time stands still, and all that's left is the gentle dance of the whisk, the quiet beauty of the matcha, and the peacefulness that fills my heart.


⁴ SERVING WITH CARE

When I serve matcha, I do so with intention. I take a moment to appreciate the vibrant green color, the delicate aroma, and the complex flavors. It's a moment to slow down, breathe deeply, and savor the beauty of the present. I bring the bowl to my nose, inhaling the delicate aroma, letting its subtle nuances transport me to a place of calm. With the first sip, the complex flavors unfold on my palate—a balance of bitterness and sweetness, umami, and a hint of grassy notes. Each sip becomes a meditation, a chance to let go of distractions and focus on the here and now. In this moment, time slows down, and all that's left is the matcha, its flavors, and the peacefulness that fills my senses.


⁵ TIPS OF THE HEART

As I prepare matcha, I remember that love is in every detail. I use a bowl that feels comfortable in my hands and whisk with care, as if I'm handling something precious. With every sip, I feel a sense of gratitude for this simple yet profound ritual. Matcha becomes more than just a drink—it's a way to cultivate love, care, and mindfulness in everyday life. In the gentle curve of the bowl, I find comfort, like holding a loved one's hand. The whisk's soft strokes become a gesture of affection, each motion a testament to the care I invest in this moment. Matcha becomes a bridge between the ordinary and the sacred, a reminder to cherish each moment and to infuse everyday life with love, care, and mindfulness. With every bowl, I cultivate a sense of presence, and in its simplicity, I find profound joy.

posts.title: Does A Yearner Poet Exist?
posts.content:
Yes, it does. A yearner poet is me—I am the yearner poet, and I yearn for you. I yearn for you in the way the sea yearns for storms despite knowing how violently the waves will break against themselves afterward. There is something catastrophic about the way I carry your existence inside me, something almost fatal in the way your name settles beneath my ribs like a second heartbeat I cannot remove. People speak of love as though it were gentle, as though it arrived softly with flowers in its hands and mercy in its mouth, but they have never loved the way I do. they have never tasted the kind of longing that turns a body into a graveyard of unfinished prayers. because loving you does not feel holy—it feels like standing barefoot inside a burning cathedral, watching devotion consume itself alive while still calling it beautiful.

Yearning has always been the oldest thing inside me, older than faith. Older than grief. Older even than my own name. it sits beneath my skin like something ancient and starving, something that claws at my ribs every time silence becomes too heavy to survive. i think some people are born untouched by it, allowed to move through the world without carrying this unbearable ache inside their chest, but i was not made that way. I was made to want endlessly. to stand at the edge of absence and still reach my hands toward it as though longing itself could resurrect what has never truly belonged to me.

And perhaps that is the curse of the yearning poet: we do not simply miss people. we become inhabited by them. They linger in us like unfinished scripture, like prayers abandoned halfway through because the mouth could no longer endure the weight of speaking them aloud. Your existence follows me everywhere, not loudly, but persistently, like the sound of distant church bells swallowed by fog. There are moments where I cannot tell whether I am remembering you or worshipping you. Perhaps there is no difference anymore. perhaps yearning itself is a religion built from absence.

I have tried to escape it before. I have tried to tear your name out of my thoughts the same way desperate believers try to purge themselves of sin, but yearning is not something that leaves quietly. It roots itself deeper the more violently you resist it. It spreads through the body like smoke filling the lungs of a burning cathedral, darkening every untouched corner until even breathing begins to feel devoted to it. And still, despite the suffocation, despite the ruin, I continue feeding it. I continue kneeling before it. Because the terrifying thing about yearning is that it hurts, and yet the pain feels sacred enough to keep.

There are nights where I think yearning is holier than fulfillment itself. Because to finally possess something is to watch the hunger end, and I do not know who I am without hunger. The yearner poet survives through the unbearable continuation of wanting. through empty hands that still tremble as though they have touched divinity moments before. Through staring into the darkness and imagining it staring back with your face hidden somewhere inside it. I do not need answers anymore. I do not need certainty. i only need the ache to remain, because without it, the silence inside me would become infinite.

Even heaven and hell begin to lose meaning after enough yearning. Heaven becomes nothing more than a distant promise of closeness, while hell becomes the endless awareness of distance. And I remain suspended somewhere between both, neither forgiven nor condemned, carrying this longing like a wound I have learned to romanticize. I think that is the most blasphemous part of all—not that I yearn, but that I have begun to cherish the suffering of it. I have begun to treat my own devastation like scripture, rereading every ache as though pain itself could bring me nearer to something divine.

Because yearning changes a person. It hollows them out slowly, beautifully, until all that remains is devotion stripped bare of dignity. It turns ordinary things into relics. a voice becomes prophecy. A memory becomes ritual. a name becomes something repeated so often it no longer sounds human, only holy. And I have repeated yours enough times that it now echoes through me like a prayer spoken inside an empty cathedral where no god has answered for centuries.

Still, I remain.

Still, I yearn.

Because I am the yearner poet, and yearning is the only thing that has ever made me feel infinite.

posts.title: An Engineer's Guide for the Physics Love
posts.content:
When you're in love—and you see the world through the lens of engineering—everything begins to feel like a system. Love isn't just emotion. It's applied physics, a set of interwoven laws, reactions, and forces that shape your inner universe with measurable precision.


STATICS

You analyze the forces acting on your heart, trying to remain balanced. you brace yourself, calculating the support reactions: how much of this feeling can your emotional frame handle before you yield? you model the moment they walk into a room and become the external load that changes everything. equilibrium? impossible. you're already shifting.


DYNAMICS

your heart is in motion. you feel acceleration, not just of your pulse, but of your thoughts, your decisions. newton's second law is now emotional law: your reaction to them is proportional to the force they exert on your world. The moment becomes kinetic, not potential anymore. you're in freefall, but it's not chaos—it's governed motion.


KINEMATICS

kinematics becomes the poetry of motion. the arc of their smile, the curve of a shared glance—it's a trajectory with meaning. displacement becomes more than spatial; it's emotional. you track the path of your growing affection like plotting motion under constant acceleration.


WORK AND ENERGY

work and energy describe the effort it takes to keep the connection strong. Every word spoken, every time spent—it's joules of effort toward an emotional bond. You're a machine with no fatigue limit, and yet you learn that conservation of energy applies here too. give too much, and you're depleted; love, like a good system, needs efficiency.


THERMODYNAMICS

thermodynamics sets in as things heat up. you exchange warmth—literal and figurative. ¹ first law: your love doesn't appear from nowhere; it's energy transformed from experiences, memories, intentions. ² second law: sometimes, you feel the entropy creeping in—the uncertainty, the distance, the misunderstandings. you engineer your way through it, insulating the bond, keeping the system closed but not isolated.


FLUID MECHANICS

love flows. communication becomes a fluid, its viscosity determined by trust. too many barriers, and you get turbulent relationships; but with alignment and clarity, it’s smooth, laminar flow. pressure builds in silence, but venting gently avoids cavitation of the heart. bernoulli’s principle reminds you: where love flows fastest, pressure may be lowest—don't take speed for strength.


ELECTROMAGNETISM 

electromagnetism pulses through every touch. the field you emit around each other is palpable— an invisible influence like a charged body drawing another close. capacitance builds when you store all the things you want to say. resistance? it's what you feel when you're not sure they feel the same. but when the circuit is closed— when you connect— it's pure current, energy flowing freely, lighting up your world.


WAVES AND OPTICS 

through waves and optics, you see and are seen. tou learn how to transmit without distortion, to resonate at the right frequency. you watch the interference patterns of your lives overlapping. reflection and refraction happen, but clarity returns when you align your lenses. love, like light, travels both as wave and particle— sometimes ethereal, sometimes solid.


MODERN PHYSICS 

you abandon certainty and embrace the quantum nature of love. you're both wavefunctions— only collapsing into certainty when observed. entanglement becomes more than a phenomenon; it becomes the explanation for how you're still affected by them across distance, time, and space.


MATERIALS SCIENCE 

materials science teaches you how you and they are made. you test each other's stress-strain behavior, learn ductility and resilience. some days, you're elastic, bouncing back from conflict; other days, you're plastic, permanently changed. the fracture point is real, but engineers design for safety— and so you learn how to reinforce each other, build stronger alloys of emotion and understanding.


CONTROL SYSTEMS

control systems come into play as your relationship grows. you identify feedback loops— positive ones that reinforce joy, and negative ones that stabilize tension. you tune your emotions like PID controllers: proportional in reaction, integrative in memory, derivative in prediction. stability is engineered, not assumed. and lastly;


ENGINEERING PHYSICS

posts.title: To the Little Girl I Never Met
posts.subtitle: She endured so much just to become the woman I get to love today.
posts.content:
I'm not just loving you for who you are and who you are becoming; I'm also loving the little girl inside you who has been through so much just to become the person you are today. I may not have known her when she was younger, and I may never know every story she carried quietly, but I wish I could have been there for her, too. I wish I could have told her that she didn't deserve every difficult thing she had to go through, that she didn't have to understand everything so soon, and that one day, she would grow into someone worth being proud of.

I wonder what she was like before the world taught her how to be strong. I wonder what made her laugh uncontrollably, what dreams she had before she started worrying about whether they were possible, and what little things made her happy before life became complicated. I wonder how many times she had to wipe her own tears, how many things she kept to herself because she didn't know who to tell, and how many moments she had to pretend that she was okay when she really wasn't.

I wish I could go back and sit beside that little girl, even if only for a moment, and tell her that she would make it here. I would tell her that the things she was going through would not be the end of her story. I would tell her that one day, she would grow up to become someone who knows how to love, how to care, how to dream, and how to keep going even when life gives her every reason to stop.

Maybe she wouldn't believe me at first.

Maybe she would wonder how someone could possibly know that things would get better.

But I would still tell her.

Because I know the person she became.

I know the woman who still wakes up every day and tries again. I know the woman who gets tired but continues anyway. I know the woman who spends so much of herself caring for other people, even when she has her own battles quietly happening in the background. I know the woman who sometimes doubts herself but still finds a way to move forward.

And knowing her makes me wish I could have known the little girl, too.

I want to love every version of you—not just the version standing in front of me now, but every version of you that had to exist before her. The child who was still learning what the world was, the girl who was trying to understand herself, the teenager who was figuring out how to survive things she never thought she would have to face, and the woman who eventually learned how to carry all those experiences with her.

None of those versions of you disappeared.

They became part of you.

And I think that's why I want to be gentle with you. Because I know there is a younger version of you somewhere inside, still carrying memories that I may never fully understand. There are parts of your past that I cannot change, wounds I cannot undo, and moments I cannot go back to protect you from.

But I can love the person who came out of them.

I can remind you that you don't have to be strong every second. I can listen when you need to talk about things that still hurt. I can celebrate the things that make you happy. I can stay beside you when you're tired. And when you forget how far you've come, I can remind you.

Because sometimes, I don't think you realize just how much that little girl accomplished by making it this far.

She survived days she probably thought she couldn't.

She grew through things that could have made her bitter.

She learned how to love despite the things that hurt her.

And somehow, she became you.

I'm not only loving the woman you became; I'm loving the little girl who had to survive long enough for me to meet her.

I think that's one of the most beautiful things about loving someone: you don't simply fall in love with who they are today. You begin to understand the pieces of their past that shaped them, the experiences that made them who they are, and the younger versions of them that still live quietly beneath everything they've become.

So if there are days when you feel like you're not doing enough, I hope you remember the little girl you once were.

She didn't know where life would take her.

She didn't know what she would become.

She didn't know all the people she would meet, all the dreams she would chase, all the things she would accomplish, or all the love she would eventually find.

But she kept going anyway.

And look at you now.

You're still here.

You're still dreaming.

You're still becoming.

And I'm so proud of you for that.

I hope you learn to look at yourself with the same gentleness that I see you with. I hope you stop being so hard on the person you are now for not having everything figured out. You have already spent so much of your life trying to become someone you could be proud of.

Maybe it's time to realize that you already are.

And if I could tell that little girl one more thing, I would tell her that she did well. She did more than well.

She became someone deeply loved.

She became someone worth staying for.

She became someone whose stories I want to hear, whose dreams I want to witness, whose happiness I want to celebrate, and whose difficult days I want to sit through.

I may never be able to meet the little girl you once were, but I can love the woman she became.

And maybe, in loving you gently today, I can give a little love to the younger you who deserved it all along.

posts.title: A Witness to Your Becoming
posts.subtitle: I have seen you struggle, I have seen you endure, and I hope I get to see you become everything you've dreamed of.
posts.content:
I have witnessed the moments when you struggled, the moments when you were exhausted, and the moments when you wanted to give up but couldn't because you still had dreams you wanted to fulfill—not for anyone else, but for yourself.

I've seen how you tried to carry things that sometimes felt far too heavy for one person. I've seen how you pushed through an entire day even when you were already exhausted, how you chose to get back up even after losing the motivation to do so, and how you convinced yourself that you could keep going even during the moments when you simply wanted to stop.

And I know that none of it has been easy for you.

There were days when it felt like the world simply refused to cooperate. There were nights filled with exhaustion and mornings when you had to get up even though all you wanted was to stay in bed. There were moments when you questioned whether you were still on the right path, whether you could keep going, and whether all the exhaustion you were giving for that dream would eventually be worth it.

But despite everything, you kept going.

And that's one of the things I admire most about you.

Not because you're always strong, but because even when you know you can get tired, you still learn to move forward. Not because you never get hurt, but because even when you do, you still choose to get back up. Not because you don't have fears, but because you don't let those fears make your decisions for you.

And I hope that when the day comes when you forget how far you've already come, you'll remember that there was someone who witnessed every step you took.

I saw the nights you stayed up late studying. I saw the days when you barely had any energy left but still had things you needed to do. I heard you rant about the things that exhausted you, and I also heard the happiness in your voice whenever there was something, no matter how small, that you were proud of.

And through every one of those moments, I admired you even more.

I don't wish for you to never feel tired again. I don't wish for you to never feel sad or discouraged either. I know those things are part of life, and I don't want to promise you a life without hardship because I know the world doesn't work that way.

All I want is for you to remember that when the days come when you feel like you can't do it anymore, you don't have to believe that you have to face everything alone.

If you need to rest, then rest.

If you need to cry, then cry.

If you need to talk about everything you've been keeping inside, tell me.

And if you have nothing left to say, we can simply sit in silence.

I won't rush you.

I won't force you to be strong right away.

I'll simply stay here while you slowly regain the strength that life has taken from you.

Because I don't want to love only the version of you who is happy, put together, and full of energy. I want to know you on the days when you're exhausted, when your thoughts are a mess, when you're full of doubts, and when you don't know how you're going to face the next day.

I want to be a witness not only to the days when you win, but also to the days when you have to fight quietly.

And when the day finally comes when you achieve the dreams you've been fighting so hard for, I want you to remember the version of yourself who almost gave up but chose to keep going.

Because you were the one who found a way to get there.

You were the one who stayed up late.

You were the one who endured.

You were the one who fought.

And you are also the one who deserves to experience all the beautiful things you're fighting for now.

So while you're walking toward your dreams, I hope you never forget to be kind to yourself.

You don't always have to be fast.

You don't always have to be excellent.

You don't always have to prove to everyone that you can do it.

Sometimes, doing the best you can on that particular day is enough.

And if the day comes when you feel like giving up again, I hope you remember that being tired doesn't mean you have to stop.

You can pause for a while.

You can breathe.

You can rest.

And when you're ready, you can continue again.

And if you ever need someone to believe in you while you're struggling to believe in yourself, I'm here.

Not to carry the entire world for you, because I know you are capable of facing your own battles.

I'm here to remind you that you don't have to face every battle alone.

I have witnessed how much you've struggled.

I've witnessed how exhausted you've become.

And someday, I want to be there to witness the day you finally say, "I did it."

And when that day comes, I hope you'll smile and look back at everything you've been through.

Because every night you thought you wouldn't make it, every tear you wiped away on your own, every exhaustion you endured, and every moment you chose to get back up when you wanted to give up—all of it became part of the journey toward the person you've always dreamed of becoming.

And when you finally reach the dream you've been chasing for so long, I hope you remember to congratulate yourself.

Because you've been fighting for a long time.

And through all those moments, even when you didn't notice, there was someone quietly admiring you.

That someone is me.

And I will always support you—not because you have to be perfect, but simply because you are you.

And that will always be enough for me.

posts.title: A Little Too Much
posts.subtitle: Maybe I worry this much because somewhere along the way, you became someone I couldn't help but care about.
posts.content:
Worrying about someone is normal, I know. But why do I worry so much with this strange hint of guilt that I can't seem to shake? It's like I don't have the right to worry, especially when I know you're okay, or at least safe until you get home. I know you're capable of taking care of yourself. I know you know what you're doing. So why does a part of me still feel uneasy whenever I don't hear from you?

Maybe I'm not even worried.

Maybe I'm just upset because I'm worried.

Or maybe I'm worried because I care too much.

I don't know anymore.

It's confusing when your mind knows there's nothing to be afraid of, but your heart still refuses to settle down. I can tell myself a hundred times that you're fine, that you'll be home soon, that there's no reason to overthink anything, and yet I still find myself checking my phone, wondering if you've gotten home, wondering how your day went, wondering if something happened that you haven't told me about.

And then I feel guilty for even feeling that way.

Because who am I to worry this much?

I'm not supposed to know every little detail of your day. I'm not supposed to expect constant updates or need reassurance every time you're out. You have your own life, your own responsibilities, your own things to do. I understand that. I really do.

But understanding something doesn't always make the feeling disappear.

Sometimes I wish I could turn it off.

I wish I could simply think, "She's okay," and leave it at that. I wish I could stop myself from looking at the time and wondering why it's taking longer than usual. I wish I could stop imagining every possible reason why you haven't replied yet, even when I know most of them are probably nothing.

Maybe you're busy.

Maybe you're tired.

Maybe you're talking to someone.

Maybe you simply put your phone down and forgot about it.

And that's okay.

I know it is.

Still, there I am, quietly waiting for that little notification that tells me you're home.

Not because I need you to explain yourself.

Not because I want to keep track of where you are.

Not because I don't trust you.

I think I just want to know that you're safe.

That's all.

Maybe that's where the guilt comes from. I worry, but I don't want my worry to become a burden to you. I care, but I don't want my care to feel like a responsibility you have to carry. I miss you, but I don't want you to feel like you always have to be available just because I happen to be waiting.

So I keep most of it to myself.

I tell myself to relax.

I tell myself you're okay.

I tell myself that caring about someone doesn't mean I have to know where they are every second of the day.

And eventually, I realize that maybe love isn't about having control over someone's safety. Maybe it's simply accepting that you can't always protect the people you love, no matter how badly you want to.

All I can do is hope you're okay.

Hope you get home safely.

Hope you had a good day.

Hope that when you finally get home, you're able to rest and forget about everything that exhausted you.

And maybe when that notification finally comes, I'll smile quietly to myself and think, "There you are."

Maybe I'll pretend I wasn't worried at all.

Maybe I'll act like I wasn't checking my phone every few minutes.

Maybe I'll simply ask, "Did you get home safely?"

And when you say yes, I'll finally breathe a little easier.

Because maybe that's what happens when you care about someone deeply enough.

Their safety becomes a small part of your peace.

Their silence becomes something you notice.

Their presence becomes something you look forward to.

And their "I'm home" becomes something that can instantly quiet a mind that has spent the last hour making up a hundred different possibilities.

I don't think I can explain exactly when it happened.

I don't know when your well-being became something my heart instinctively worried about.

Maybe it happened slowly, somewhere between our late-night calls, your stories about your day, the little things you tell me, and all the moments we've shared.

Maybe I just started caring before I realized I was already caring this much.

And maybe that's why I'm worried.

Not because I think you're incapable of taking care of yourself.

Not because I don't trust you.

But because somewhere along the way, you became someone I genuinely want to see safe, happy, and home at the end of every day.

So maybe I'm not upset.

Maybe I'm not guilty for worrying.

Maybe I'm just learning what it feels like to love someone enough that a simple "I'm home" can mean more to me than you realize.

And if that's what caring too much feels like, then I suppose I'll have to learn how to carry it gently.

posts.title: Tell Me Everything
posts.subtitle: For the nurse who spends her days caring for everyone else, and deserves someone to listen to her, too.
posts.content:
I used to think that loving someone meant being there for the happiest moments—the celebrations, the late-night laughter, the little victories, and all the beautiful things that make life feel lighter. I thought love was supposed to be loud sometimes, something you could easily recognize in grand gestures and carefully chosen words.

But the more I get to know you, the more I realize that maybe love can also be quiet.

Maybe love is sitting on the other end of the phone while you tell me about your day. Maybe it's listening to the same story you've already told me before and still letting you tell it again. Maybe it's remembering the little things you casually mention and asking about them later. Maybe it's simply being there when the excitement fades and all that's left is exhaustion.

And maybe, for me, loving you means choosing to stay through all of it.

I witnessed all your struggles every day, and I still choose to love you gently. Like what I've said, life has already been so hard on us. At the very least, if listening to your rants and hearing about what happened throughout your day—whether something good or bad happened along the way—is what you need, then I'll gladly be here to listen.

It doesn't matter if you have so much to yap about. I don't mind how long your stories get, how many times you repeat the same thing, or how many little details you want to tell me. All I think about is that maybe you just need someone to listen to your rants, your stories, your frustrations, or even the most random thoughts that cross your mind.

And I don't mind if you're tired, overwhelmed, irritated, or having one of those days when everything seems to go wrong. I don't mind if all you want to do is complain about how exhausting your day was. I don't need you to make your stories sound interesting, and you don't have to pretend that everything is okay when it isn't. You can tell me about the good days, but you can also give me the bad ones.

I want to know both.

I want to hear about the little things that made you smile, the things that made you laugh, the moments that made your heart feel light, and even the things that made you want to cry at the end of the day. I want to know what made you happy and what made you upset. I want to hear you say, "I had such a terrible day," and still be able to remind you that tomorrow might be a little kinder.

Because loving you, for me, isn't only about being there when everything is beautiful.

It's also about staying when things aren't.

I know I can't take away every difficult thing you have to face. I can't magically make your responsibilities disappear, make your exhaustion go away, or fix every problem that comes your way. Sometimes, all I can really do is listen. Sometimes, all I can offer is my time, my attention, and a place where you can let everything out without worrying about being too much.

And if that's all you need from me, then that's enough.

You never have to apologize for talking too much. You never have to wonder if you're bothering me. You never have to filter yourself just because you think your problems are too small or your stories are too long. If something matters to you, then it matters to me too—not because I have to understand every little thing, but because I love you enough to want to understand the things that matter to you.

I want to be the person you can call after a long day and say, "I have a story to tell about what happened to me earlier," without hesitation.

I want to be the person you can tell about the smallest victory you had that day, even if it seems insignificant to everyone else. I want to celebrate the little things with you, too, because I know that sometimes the smallest wins are the ones that keep us going.

And if you come to me with nothing but exhaustion, I'll stay.

If you come to me with a hundred stories, I'll listen.

If you come to me laughing, I'll laugh with you.

If you come to me crying, I'll stay until you've said everything you need to say.

You don't always have to be strong around me.

You don't always have to be the nurse who knows how to care for everyone else. You don't always have to be the one who knows what to do, what to say, or how to make everything better.

Sometimes, you can just be you.

And let someone take care of you for a while.

Maybe that's one of the ways I want to love you—with patience, with understanding, and with gentleness. Not because I think you're fragile, but because I know how much you carry every day, even when you don't talk about it.

So if life gets too loud, come to me.

If your day gets too heavy, tell me about it.

If you have too much to say, yap as much as you want.

I'll be here.

I'll listen to the stories you've told me a hundred times and the ones you're telling me for the first time. I'll listen to the things that make you happy and the things that make you want to scream. I'll listen even when there isn't really a point to the story, because sometimes you don't need someone to solve anything.

Sometimes, you just need someone who stays long enough to hear you say it all.

And I want to be that someone for you.

Because I don't only want to love the version of you that is happy, well-rested, and having a good day.

I want to love you on the days when you're exhausted, frustrated, messy, emotional, and completely overwhelmed, too.

I want to know you in your softness and in your chaos.

And no matter how difficult the day has been, I hope you always remember that you have someone who will gladly listen to you at the end of it.

Even if all you have to say is, "Today was terrible."

I'll still answer, "Okay, tell me everything."

posts.title: Can I Call You When I Get Home?
posts.subtitle: I used to hate phone calls, but now, they're my favorite.
posts.content:
I hate phone calls, but you're the exception. 

Before I met you, I never understood how people could spend hours talking on the phone. I always thought they were exhausting. I'd rather send a message than answer a call. It felt easier that way—quieter, simpler, and less overwhelming. I never imagined that one person could completely change the way I looked at something I used to avoid.

Then I met you.

Whether you call me at night after you've gotten home or while you're busy with something—studying; reviewing for a demo, quiz, or exam; organizing your notes; or even doing your makeup—I always look forward to hearing from you. Somehow, without me even realizing it, phone calls with you have become my favorite part of the day.

I love hearing your voice. I love it when you randomly start singing, even if it's only for a few seconds. I love listening to you tell me stories about your day—about your duties, the little things that made you smile, the moments that exhausted you, or the random thoughts that crossed your mind. Somehow, even the stories you think are ordinary become my favorite ones simply because they're yours. And no matter how your day goes, you always ask me about mine, even though my answer is almost always, "Nothing much happened."

But the truth is, something always does happen. I get to hear your voice, and somehow, that's enough to make an ordinary day feel a little less ordinary.

It's funny because I've always preferred silence. I enjoy being alone, and I've always believed silence was enough for me. But with you, silence feels different. It isn't empty, and it certainly isn't awkward. It's peaceful.

Sometimes, we don't even have anything important to talk about. Sometimes, we're simply there, keeping each other company without saying much at all. You study while I quietly do my own thing. I scroll through my phone while you review your notes. Sometimes you hum a song under your breath without realizing it. Sometimes we tease each other over the smallest things until one of us starts laughing. And sometimes, we sit in complete silence, yet somehow, it never feels uncomfortable.

I've learned that silence doesn't always mean there's nothing left to say. Sometimes, it simply means you've found someone you're comfortable enough to say nothing with. And somehow, I found that person in you.

Then there are nights when neither of us notices how late it's become. What feels like a few minutes somehow turns into hours. We tell ourselves we'll end the call after one more story, one more joke, or one more question, but "one more" never really means one more.

Sometimes, we even fall asleep while the call is still going. Those moments might seem ordinary to everyone else, but they're among my favorites. Waking up in the middle of the night, hearing your soft breathing on the other end of the line, and realizing neither of us remembered to hang up somehow makes me smile before I drift back to sleep. It's such a simple thing, yet it brings me a kind of comfort I never knew I needed.

I never thought a phone call could feel like home, but yours somehow does.

I think that's my favorite part about us. You never have to try too hard. You don't have to say anything extraordinary, and you don't have to entertain me every second we're on the phone. Your presence has always been enough, and maybe that's what love looks like. Not always in grand confessions or dramatic gestures, but in hearing someone's sleepy voice before they drift off, listening to them breathe while the world grows quiet around you, or staying on the phone even when neither of you has anything left to say because simply being there is enough.

Maybe that's why I never get tired of your calls. Every time my phone lights up with your name, I still smile before answering because I already know that, for the next few hours, the world will become a little quieter, a little lighter, and a little easier to carry.

You have no idea how much comfort your voice brings me. You have no idea how many ordinary days you've unknowingly made beautiful just by calling. You have no idea how someone who once hated phone calls now secretly hopes you'll call again before the day ends.

And maybe that's the funniest part of all.

I thought I hated phone calls. Turns out, I was just waiting for the right person to be on the other end of the line.

Because no matter what we're talking about—or even if we're talking about nothing at all—as long as it's you, I'll always answer. And if one day we accidentally fall asleep before saying goodnight again, I hope we never apologize for it. Because somehow, even in sleep, knowing you're still there makes the distance between us feel a little smaller.

Maybe that's why your voice has become my favorite sound. Not because it's perfect, but because somehow, it always feels like home.

As I ponder these questions, I'm drawn into a labyrinth of self-discovery, a maze of mirrors reflecting the complexities of the human condition.


I'm forced to confront the darkest corners of my own psyche, the shadowy recesses where my deepest fears and desires reside. And there, in the depths of my own soul, I find a glimmer of understanding. I realize that the phrase is not just a literal description but a metaphorical one. It's a symbol of the self-destructive tendencies that lurk within us all, the impulses that drive us to consume ourselves, to devour our own hearts and minds. And yet, it's also a testament to the human capacity for resilience, for adaptation, for finding sustenance in the most unexpected places.


Ultimately, the phrase becomes a reflection of my own complicated relationship with myself, a reminder that I am both the consumer and the consumed, the eater and the eaten. I am the flesh that I devour and the hunger that I satisfy.

posts.title: A Letter I Never Sent to My Younger Self
posts.subtitle: Written the week I turned the same age my mother was when she had me.
posts.content:
You won't believe this, but you're going to be fine. Not in the loud, certain way people say it to make you stop crying—fine in the quieter way, the way a room is fine after you've lived in it long enough to stop noticing the crack in the ceiling. 

I know you think the version of yourself you're supposed to become is already decided, waiting somewhere up ahead like a train you have to catch. It isn't. You will miss trains. You will miss the one you thought was the only one. And somehow you'll still arrive somewhere worth arriving at, just later, and by a route nobody would have recommended.

You are so afraid of being ordinary that you can't yet see how much tenderness is hiding inside an ordinary life. The dishes in the sink. The friend who calls on a Tuesday for no reason. These will matter more than the things you're currently losing sleep over—I promise you this; it's the way you can only promise something after you've already lived past it.

There is a particular kind of loneliness you're carrying right now that feels like evidence of something being wrong with you. It isn't. It's just what it feels like to be a person who notices too much and says too little. That noticing, eventually, becomes the thing people love you for. Be patient with it.

You will hurt people without meaning to, and you will be hurt in ways you didn't see coming. Neither will be the end of the story you think it is. Both will be folded, eventually, into a life that has room for all of it—the mistakes, the almosts, the ones that got away, and the one who didn't.

I'm not writing to warn you. I'm writing because I finally understand what my mother must have felt at my age, holding a version of me that hadn't happened yet, and I wanted, just once, to hold you the same way—without trying to fix you, just glad you're going to make it.

posts.title: Becoming My Own Safe Haven
posts.content:
In the quiet moments, when the world seems to fade into the background, it's easy to forget that the most steadfast ally you have is yourself. Amidst the noise of external validation and the retreat and flow of support from others, there's a profound strength in self-reliance. It's the realization that the most consistent and enduring support comes not from the voices around you but from the voice within.


To support oneself is to stand firm on the bedrock of personal conviction, to trust in one's own resilience, and to draw strength from the depths of one's spirit. It's about embracing the journey, with all its uncertainties, and finding the courage to move forward, even when the path ahead is shrouded in darkness. Self-support is the quiet confidence that comes from knowing you've weathered storms before and can do so again.


In a world that often measures worth by external standards, supporting oneself is a radical act of self-love and acceptance. It's about validating your own experiences, honoring your emotions, and affirming your worth, irrespective of external opinions. When you learn to be your own rock, your own safe haven, you become unshakeable.


This isn't to say that support from others isn't valuable or welcome—it's simply to acknowledge that true stability comes from within. When you cultivate a strong relationship with yourself, you build a foundation that no external circumstance can erode. You become your own shelter in the storm, your own beacon in the darkness.


So, stand tall with yourself. Be your own confidant, your own cheerleader, and your own guardian. in the silence, listen for the voice that whispers. 

ㅤㅤㅤㅤ


you are enough.


ㅤㅤㅤㅤ

Trust in your strength, believe in your worth, and know that no matter what, you'll always have yourself to rely on.

posts.title: A Gentle Reminder to Enjoy Life
posts.subtitle: Enjoy the Journey
posts.content:
Life isn't easy. You need to understand things that are hard to understand and accept those things that are hard to accept. Life isn't a smooth ride, but at least you can choose to enjoy it. It's a journey of twists and turns, of laughter and tears, of triumphs and setbacks. But amidst the chaos, there's a simple truth—you just need to enjoy it. Find beauty in the broken, joy in the journey, and laughter in the mess. It's not about being naive or ignoring the struggles—it's about finding the silver lining, the lessons learned, and the growth that comes with every fall.


Savor the sweetness of a sunrise, the warmth of a loved one's smile, and the quiet peace of a still moment. It's not about having it all together—it's about finding happiness in the little things. It's about finding joy in the journey, not just the destination. It's about embracing the imperfections, the uncertainties, and the unknowns. Life's too short to be weighed down by worries and fears.


So, take a deep breath, put on a smile, and face whatever comes next. A good cup of coffee, a great book, or a walk in the park—these are the things that make life worth living. Because in the end, it's not about the destination but the journey—the people we meet, the lessons we learn, and the moments we cherish.

posts.title: To the Nursing Student I Met at Midnight
posts.subtitle: A love story written between late-night conversations and unspoken feelings.
posts.content:
On a random midnight, I never realized that I would find you. 

It was just another ordinary night. We talked. We shared our own stories. We laughed. And somehow, everything felt so unreal. It's funny how I ended our conversation that night because I thought you might find me annoying with all the things I had said. But then, after a couple of days, we talked again—and this time, we clicked. 

We started talking every day and every night. We stayed up late simply because we enjoyed each other's company. We talked again. We laughed again. We shared our stories again—whether they were filled with happiness or weighed down by sadness. We didn't just exchange stories; we slowly tied our souls together until they felt like one. And I admit that was the first time I had ever experienced something like that—meeting someone who understood my soul and saw parts of themselves in it. I loved that feeling. It felt like I had finally found a place where I didn't have to explain why I am the way I am.

But I know, and I'm aware that's not how it works. No one is made to understand another person completely. We're all different. We carry different fears, different scars, different dreams, and different ways of loving. And maybe that's what makes it so beautiful.

Because despite all those differences, you still chose to stay.

You stayed through my random thoughts at two in the morning. You listened to stories that had no ending. You laughed at jokes that weren't even funny. You made room for every version of me—the loud one, the quiet one, and the one who simply wanted to sit in comfortable silence.

Without realizing it, you became part of my routine.

My day somehow felt incomplete if I didn't get to tell you about the smallest things that happened. Every notification made me hope it was you. Every midnight became something I looked forward to because I knew there was a chance I'd get to spend it with you. Somehow, the hours never felt enough. No matter how long we talked, I'd always find another story to tell, another question to ask, another reason to stay awake a little longer if it meant spending more time with you.

I would have never imagined that because of that one random night, I would have a nurse by my side.

It's funny how life works. Out of all the people I could have met that midnight, it led me to you. Someone whose hands are meant to heal, yet somehow ended up healing parts of me you never even knew were hurting. I never expected that a random conversation would become my favorite part of every day or that the person I once thought I might annoy would become the person I couldn't wait to talk to.

It's strange how love doesn't always arrive with grand confessions or dramatic moments. Sometimes, it quietly grows from calling each other "Baby" as a joke until it no longer feels like one. Sometimes, it hides in shared laughter, in comfortable silences, and in remembering the little things about each other. Sometimes, it begins on an ordinary midnight that was never supposed to be memorable.

And maybe that's how I fell for you.

Not all at once, but little by little.

Conversation after conversation.

Midnight, after midnight.

Until one day, I caught myself smiling at my phone before I even opened your message. Until your name became my favorite notification. Until your presence started feeling less like coincidence and more like something I silently thanked the universe for.

Sometimes I catch myself smiling just thinking about how everything started. If I had gone to sleep a little earlier, if you had never sent that message, or if one of us had decided not to interact, maybe our paths would have never crossed. But

They did.

And now, every midnight reminds me of the night I found you—the nurse who unknowingly became the calm in my chaos, the comfort in my restless thoughts, and the person who made me believe that the best things in life don't always come with a plan.

I don't know what tomorrow has planned for us. I don't know where these late-night conversations will eventually lead. But if I could choose one place to be right now, it would still be here—with you, talking about everything and nothing, letting another midnight pass without ever noticing the time.

Because somehow, every midnight has become my favorite part of the day.

It's where I found you.

And if I'm lucky enough, maybe it's where I'll continue falling in love with you, over and over again.

posts.title: If My Younger Self Read This
posts.subtitle: The person you’re trying so hard to become has been quietly cheering for you all along.
posts.content:
Dear younger me, 

You always believed that one day, everything would make sense.

You thought there would come a morning when you’d wake up and suddenly know who you were, what you wanted, and where you belonged. You imagined adulthood as a destination—a place where confusion no longer existed.

I'm writing to tell you that it doesn’t quite happen that way.

You don’t magically become fearless. You don’t stop making mistakes. You don’t suddenly understand life just because you’ve grown older.

But somehow, you become softer with yourself.

You'll spend years trying to earn everyone’s approval before realizing that no amount of validation can replace the peace that comes from accepting yourself. You'll overthink conversations that everyone else has already forgotten. You'll apologize for taking up space, even when you’ve done nothing wrong.

I wish I could tell you not to.

not because life will be easy, but because you’ll eventually learn that your worth was never something other people had the authority to decide.

There will be friendships that feel permanent until they aren’t.

People you thought would stay forever will quietly become strangers. At first, you’ll think it’s your fault—that maybe if you had been funnier, kinder, quieter, louder, or simply “more,” they would have stayed.

They wouldn’t have.

some people are only meant to walk beside you for a chapter, not the whole story. their leaving isn’t always a reflection of your value. sometimes it’s simply how life unfolds.

You'll also discover that growing up means grieving versions of yourself.

You'll miss the child who laughed without worrying about how she looked. You'll miss the teenager who believed love could fix everything. You'll miss old dreams that no longer fit the person you’re becoming.

It's okay to miss them.

You don’t have to hate who you used to be in order to appreciate who you’re becoming.

And here’s something no one tells you: healing isn’t dramatic.

It's choosing to get out of bed on difficult mornings. It's learning not to send the message you typed in the middle of the night. It's forgiving yourself for things you didn’t know then. It's noticing that the memories no longer hurt the way they once did.

Healing often arrives so quietly that you don’t realize you’ve changed until one day, something that used to break you barely touches your heart.

You'll learn that love isn’t supposed to make you shrink.

The right people won’t ask you to become less emotional, less ambitious, or less yourself just to make them comfortable. Real love makes room for your honesty. Real friendship doesn’t make you question whether you’re enough.

Please don’t spend your life chasing people who have already decided not to choose you.

Choose yourself, too.

And while you’re at it, keep writing.

Write even when no one is reading.

Write when you’re happy, because joy deserves to be remembered.

Write when you’re heartbroken, because pain becomes lighter once it has somewhere to go.

write because one day you’ll look back at these words and realize they were never just pages—they were proof that you survived every version of yourself.

You won’t have all the answers.

Honestly, I hope you never do.

because life isn’t measured by how quickly you figure everything out. It's measured by how willing you are to keep learning, keep loving, and keep beginning again.

So be patient.

One day you’ll understand that becoming isn’t about finding yourself.

It's about creating yourself, little by little, through every choice you make.

And if you ever feel lost, remember this:

the person you’re trying so hard to become has been quietly cheering for you all along.

With love,

Your older self.

posts.title: Make A Reading Habit
posts.subtitle: Not every story is printed on paper.
posts.content:
They say, "Make a reading habit.”  

So, I did. 

At first, I thought it meant books. Pages. Chapters. Margins filled with notes and passages underlined in haste because I was afraid I'd forget how they made me feel. But reality has a different curriculum.

When you step outside the comfort of paper and ink, you realize that life requires a different kind of reading. You don’t just read books anymore—you read people. You read the way someone answers a simple question. You read the pauses that stretch a little too long. You read the smiles that don’t quite reach the eyes. You read the things people say and the things they spend a lifetime avoiding.

You learn that every person carries a language of their own.

Some speak through words. Others through actions. And others through silence. Some tell you exactly who they are. Others leave clues scattered everywhere, hoping someone will be patient enough to piece them together.

And so, without noticing, I developed a reading habit.

I began reading with tired eyes and restless hands. I read affection disguised as teasing, grief behind humor, and loneliness buried beneath a crowded room. I read people who wanted to be understood and people who spent years making themselves impossible to understand.

The strange thing is that people are far more complicated than any book I’ve ever held.

A novel eventually reaches its final chapter. Every mystery is solved. Every question is answered. The story ends.

While people don’t.

And that’s why reading people is so difficult.

because we’re all unfinished manuscripts.

drafts upon drafts of who we were, who we are, and who we’re trying to become.

Yet we keep writing.

So when people tell me to make a reading habit, I think I've done exactly that.

I read every day.

Not always from the book, but from the world around me.

from conversations.

from goodbyes.

from fleeting moments.

from the stories people carry within them.

because life, I’ve learned, is an endless library filled with unfinished books. and every person you meet is a story still being written.

including yourself.

settings.aboutContent:
I've kept some form of journal since 2020, mostly out of necessity rather than discipline—I've always needed to write things down before I fully understood how I felt about them.

The name comes from the only way I've ever been able to write anything honest: by half-convincing myself no one would actually read it. If No One Reads This is what happened when I got tired of being the only reader of things I suspected other people might need too.

I'm not trying to have the last word on anything. I'm just trying to say the true thing before I forget what it felt like.

What you'll find here is a mix: letters, personal reflections, journal entries kept mostly intact, a handful of poems, and short stories that are fiction in name only.

I don't publish on a schedule. I publish when something has finished the slow work of becoming a sentence instead of just a feeling. If you're here, I'm glad. There's no rush to any of this.
